definition_zh: 组成；构成；成分；作文；作曲；作品；构图；化合物；（印刷）排版；和解协议
definition_en: the parts or ingredients that make up something; the act of putting things together; a written or musical work; the arrangement of elements in an image
core_image: 不同的颜料被一笔笔放到画布上，最后成为一幅有结构的画
scene: 这篇作文的优点是结构清楚：开头、论证、反例、结论，各占其位。 The strength of this composition is its clear structure: opening, argument, counter-example and conclusion each hold their place.
sceneCN: 这里 composition 是「作文、写作作品」（第 2 个义项：学生或作者写成的文章）；句意：这篇作文的优点是结构清楚：开头、论证、反例、结论各占其位。图中可辨识物件：稿纸、钢笔、画布与颜料、乐谱、结构提纲。

pos.zh: 组成；构成；成分；作品；作文
作曲；构图；排版；和解协议

senses.title: The parts that make something up
senses.definition: the parts or ingredients of which something consists
senses.definitionCN: 某物由以构成的各部分或成分
senses.example: the composition of the atmosphere
senses.exampleCN: 大气的成分
senses.why: This is the analytic sense: the whole is asked to give an account of its parts. It is not the act of making but the make-up that results, and it is usually stated in percentages or proportions.
senses.whyCN: 这是分析义：要求整体交代其部分。它不是制造动作，而是由此形成的构成，通常以百分比或比例陈述。

senses.title: A written exercise
senses.definition: a short piece of writing done as an exercise, especially by a student
senses.definitionCN: 作为练习写成的短篇文章，尤指学生所作
senses.example: She wrote a composition on her hometown.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一篇关于家乡的作文。
senses.why: School usage narrows the word to a set task. The composition is judged on organization as much as content, which is why the same noun also names the arrangement of parts.
senses.whyCN: 学校用法把词收窄为规定任务。作文既评内容也评组织，故同一名词也指部分的安排。

senses.title: A musical work
senses.definition: a piece of music, or the art of writing one
senses.definitionCN: 一部音乐作品，或写作音乐的艺术
senses.example: The symphony is his finest composition.
senses.exampleCN: 这部交响曲是他最好的作品。
senses.why: Music turns 'putting together' into an art: notes, rhythms, and sections are composed into a whole. The composer is literally one who puts together, and the work is the result.
senses.whyCN: 音乐把“放在一起”变成艺术：音符、节奏与段落被组合成整体。composer 字面即“组合者”，作品是结果。

senses.title: Arrangement in an image
senses.definition: the arrangement of elements within a picture or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 画面或照片中各元素的安排
senses.example: The photograph's composition leads the eye to the door.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片的构图把视线引向门口。
senses.why: Visual art uses the word for the deliberate placement of forms. Composition is not the subject but the order that makes the subject readable, and it can be judged apart from what is depicted.
senses.whyCN: 视觉艺术用该词指形式的刻意布置。构图不是题材，而是使题材可读的秩序，且可脱离所画内容被评价。

senses.title: Chemical composition
senses.definition: the identity and proportion of substances in a material
senses.definitionCN: 材料中物质的种类与比例
senses.example: The lab analysed the water's chemical composition.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室分析了水的化学组成。
senses.why: Chemistry makes the parts measurable: elements and ratios. A change of composition is a change of substance, so the word can mark a boundary between one material and another.
senses.whyCN: 化学使部分可测：元素与比例。组成改变即物质改变，故该词可标记一种材料与另一种的边界。

senses.title: Typesetting
senses.definition: the arrangement of type and images on a page before printing
senses.definitionCN: 印刷前页面中文字与图像的安排
senses.example: The printer checked the composition of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷工检查了页面排版。
senses.why: Printing is an industrial cousin of sense 04: elements are placed in a fixed frame. The word names the stage before impression, when the page is still only an arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 印刷是第 4 义的工业表亲：元素被置于固定框内。该词命名压印之前的阶段，页面此时仍只是安排。

senses.title: A settlement with creditors
senses.definition: an agreement by which a debtor pays part of a debt and the rest is discharged
senses.definitionCN: 债务人偿还部分债务、其余被免除的协议
senses.example: The firm reached a composition with its creditors.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司与债权人达成和解协议。
senses.why: Insolvency law uses composition for a voluntary arrangement. The parties 'compose' their differences, which links the legal sense to the older sense of settling a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 破产法用 composition 指自愿安排。各方“compose”其分歧，把法律义与更早的“平息争执”义连起来。

senses.title: Word formation by combining
senses.definition: the formation of a word by joining two or more existing words
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多现有词结合成新词
senses.example: 'Blackbird' is a composition of 'black' and 'bird'.
senses.exampleCN: blackbird 是 black 与 bird 的复合。
senses.why: Linguistics uses the word for compounding. The parts remain recognizable, which distinguishes composition from derivation, where an affix is added and the base may change shape.
senses.whyCN: 语言学用该词指复合构词。各部分仍可辨识，这区别于加缀派生——后者加词缀，词基可能变形。

senses.title: A whole work of art
senses.definition: a complete artistic or literary work considered as an integrated whole
senses.definitionCN: 被视为整合整体的完整艺术或文学作品
senses.example: The composition balances light and shadow.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅作品平衡了光与影。
senses.why: The sense shifts from the act to the finished object. A composition is judged as a whole, and its quality lies in the relation of parts rather than in any part alone.
senses.whyCN: 此义从动作转向成品。作品作为整体被评价，其质量在部分关系中，而非任何单独部分。

intro.en: Composition is compose plus -ition, from Latin compositio. Compose comes from Old French composer 'put together', from Latin componere, com- 'together' plus ponere 'place'. The literal image is placing things side by side into one arrangement. The same stem gives component, composite, and compost; compost looks like a close relative and is one, but it took a separate path through 'mixed dung' to its modern garden sense.
intro.cn: composition 是 compose 加 -ition，出自拉丁 compositio。compose 出自古法语 composer“放在一起”，源于拉丁 componere，即 com-“一起”加 ponere“放置”。字面意象是把事物并排放成一个安排。同一词干给出 component、composite 与 compost；compost 看似近亲且确为近亲，但它经“混合粪肥”走上另一条路，才到现代园艺义。

items.en: ponere means 'to place, put'; it gives component, deposit, impose, and postpone.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放置、放”，给出 component、deposit、impose、postpone。

items.en: componere is com- 'together' plus ponere: to put several things into one place or order.
items.cn: componere 是 com-“一起”加 ponere：把数物放到一处或一个秩序中。

items.en: compositio 'a putting together, arrangement' is the action noun behind English composition.
items.cn: compositio“放在一起、安排”是英语 composition 背后的动作名词。

items.en: Old French composer broadens the verb to arranging, writing, and settling, and English takes it in the 14C.
items.cn: 古法语 composer 把动词拓宽到安排、写作与平息，英语于十四世纪引入。

items.en: The musical sense 'a piece composed' becomes established, along with composer for the writer of music.
items.cn: 十八世纪“写成的乐曲”义确立，composer 也固定指音乐写作者。

items.en: Chemistry, printing, law, and linguistics each fix a technical sense, while the school 'composition' remains the everyday one.
items.cn: 化学、印刷、法律与语言学各固定一个技术义，学校“作文”仍是日常义。

note.en: The first group is the compose family, including the look-alike compost; the second is words for make-up and arrangement, which differ in whether they name parts, structure, or the finished work.
note.cn: 第一组是 compose 词族，含近形词 compost；第二组是“构成与安排”类词，差别在于指部分、结构还是成品。

entries.definition: to put together; to write music or text; to calm oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 组成；创作；使平静。

entries.definition: one who writes music.
entries.definitionCN: 作曲家。

entries.definition: made of separate parts combined; a combined whole.
entries.definitionCN: 复合的；合成物。

entries.definition: the arrangement and relation of parts. It stresses organization rather than ingredients.
entries.definitionCN: 部分的安排与关系。强调组织，而非成分。

entries.definition: the composition or character of something, often informal.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的构成或性质，常口语。

entries.definition: the way things are placed or ordered. It is the act or result of placing, without the chemical or artistic weight.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被放置或排序的方式。是放置的动作或结果，不带化学或艺术分量。

normalIntro.en: Real links: ponere 'place', componere 'put together', compositio, and the separate path of compost.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：ponere“放置”、componere“放在一起”、compositio，以及 compost 的独立路径。

normal.en: Componere is 'place together'. Composition is the placing, and then the thing placed.
normal.cn: componere 是“放在一起”。composition 先是放置动作，后是放成之物。

normal.en: Ponere 'place' is visible in component, deposit, and postpone; all are about putting somewhere.
normal.cn: ponere“放置”见于 component、deposit、postpone；全都关于放到某处。

normal.en: The composer puts notes together; the student puts sentences together. One noun covers both.
normal.cn: 作曲家把音符放在一起；学生把句子放在一起。一个名词覆盖两者。

normal.en: Compost is a relative that went to the garden: same 'put together', but through mixed organic matter.
normal.cn: compost 是去了菜园的亲戚：同样“放在一起”，但经由混合有机物。

normal.en: A composition is judged as a whole; its quality is in the relations, not the parts.
normal.cn: 作品作为整体被评价；质量在关系中，不在部分里。

abstract.en: Composition is both an act and a result, which is why the same word can name a process, a text, and a material's make-up.
abstract.cn: composition 既是动作也是结果，故同一词可命名过程、文本与材料构成。

abstract.en: Every whole is a claim about which parts matter and how they should be ordered.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都是关于“哪些部分重要、应如何排序”的主张。

abstract.en: A composition can be analysed into parts, but its effect often disappears when it is; the whole is not the sum.
abstract.cn: 作品可被分析为部分，但其效果常在分析中消失；整体不是总和。

examples.en: The composition of the soil affects what will grow.
examples.cn: 土壤的组成影响能种什么。

examples.en: He wrote a composition about his first trip abroad.
examples.cn: 他写了一篇关于初次出国的作文。

examples.en: The painting's composition places the figure off-centre.
examples.cn: 这幅画的构图把人物放在偏离中心处。

dict_mnemonic.text: “康波吉申”——把零件 com 一起 pose（放）好 → composition 组成/作品

root: compose（古法语 composer ← 拉丁 componere“放在一起”= com-“一起”+ ponere“放置”）+ -ition（拉丁 compositio）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of composition: make-up, a school essay, a musical work, visual arrangement, chemical content, typesetting, a creditors' settlement, word compounding, and a finished whole. The thread is placing parts into an order.
sensesIntro.cn: composition 的九个义项：构成、作文、音乐作品、构图、化学组成、排版、债权人和解、复合构词、完整作品。共同线索是把部分放入一个秩序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pigments laid stroke by stroke onto a canvas until an ordered picture appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：颜料一笔笔落到画布上，直到出现有秩序的画。

branches.en: THE MAKE-UP: atmospheric and chemical composition ask what parts, in what ratio.
branches.cn: 构成：大气与化学组成问的是哪些部分、何种比例。

branches.en: THE WORK: essay, music, and finished art are arrangements made to be read or heard as wholes.
branches.cn: 作品：作文、音乐与成品艺术都是作为整体被读或听的安排。

branches.en: THE FRAME: painting and typesetting place elements inside a fixed visual field.
branches.cn: 框：绘画与排版把元素放进固定视觉场。

branches.en: THE SETTLEMENT: parties compose their differences by arranging a payment.
branches.cn: 和解：各方通过安排偿付来 compose 分歧。

branches.en: THE WORD: compounding puts existing words together into a new one.
branches.cn: 词：复合把现有词放在一起成新词。

intro.en: Composition is compose + -ition, from Latin compositio. Compose is componere, com- plus ponere 'place'. The family includes composer, compositional, composite, component, and the look-alike compost; all inherit the 'put together' image.
intro.cn: composition 是 compose 加 -ition，出自拉丁 compositio。compose 是 componere（com- 加 ponere“放置”）。词族含 composer、compositional、composite、component 与近形词 compost；都继承“放在一起”的意象。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'place' gives componere 'put together' and compositio 'arrangement'. English keeps -ition and builds composer, composite, and component on related stems. Compost comes through Old French compost from compositum, but its sense narrowed to mixed organic matter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere“放置”给出 componere“放在一起”与 compositio“安排”。英语保留 -ition，并在相关词干上造 composer、composite、component。compost 经古法语 compost 出自 compositum，但词义收窄为混合有机物。

definition_zh: 自动机；机器人；动作机械、毫无主见的人
definition_en: a machine that moves by itself; also, a person who acts mechanically, without thinking or feeling
core_image: 上紧发条就自己动起来的机关人偶
scene: 工位上敲了一整天相同按键，他觉得自己快成了机器。 After years on the line he worked like an automaton.
sceneCN: 这里 automaton 指「动作机械、不动脑的人」（第 2 个义项：比喻机械的人）；句意：在流水线干了多年，他干活已像机器人一般。

pos.zh: 自动机；机器人；机械行事的人

collocations.zh: 会下棋的自动机（如土耳其行弈傀儡）
没有主见的政坛机器人

derivatives.zh: 自动的；无意识的（同族词）
使自动化（automatic 回构动词）
自动机理论（计算机科学术语，复数形式保留）

senses.title: A self-moving machine
senses.definition: a mechanical figure or device that appears to move by its own power
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛凭自身动力运动的机械人偶或装置
senses.example: The museum's eighteenth-century automaton writes poems with a quill.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆那台 18 世纪的机关人偶能用羽毛笔写诗。
senses.why: The Greek automatos means self-moving; the word names any machine that seems to act alone.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 automatos 意为「自行运动」；这个词命名一切看似自主运作的机械。

senses.title: A person acting mechanically
senses.definition: a person who acts without thinking, will, or feeling, as if wound up like a machine
senses.definitionCN: 不假思索、没有意志或情感，如上发条般行事的人
senses.example: Slogging through the same routine, he felt like an automaton.
senses.exampleCN: 日复一日重复同样的例行公事，他觉得自己像台机器。
senses.why: Once machines imitated people, people who stopped thinking could be called machines back.
senses.whyCN: 机器一旦模仿了人，不再思考的人便被反称为机器。

senses.title: Automatic devices in engineering
senses.definition: any self-regulating mechanism, from clockwork to feedback systems
senses.definitionCN: 从钟表机械到反馈系统的各种自调节机构
senses.example: The temple doors of Heron of Alexandria were famous automatons.
senses.exampleCN: 亚历山大城的希伦所造神庙自动门是著名的自动装置。
senses.why: Ancient engineers already built self-acting machines, and the old word still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 古代工程师早已造出自动机械，这个古老的词至今仍然适用。

senses.title: In mathematics and computing
senses.titleCN: 数学与计算机中的自动机
senses.definition: an abstract model of computation, such as a finite automaton
senses.definitionCN: 计算的抽象模型，如有限自动机
senses.example: A finite automaton accepts or rejects strings of symbols.
senses.exampleCN: 有限自动机接受或拒绝符号串。
senses.why: Computer science needed a precise name for abstract machines that act by rule alone.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学需要一个精确的名字来指称纯粹按规则运行的抽象机器。

senses.title: Robots and androids
senses.definition: a robot, especially one built in human form, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 机器人，尤指人形机械，见于较旧或文学用法
senses.example: The novel imagined automatons serving breakfast in every home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说想象家家都有机器人备好早餐。
senses.why: Before robot was coined in 1920, automaton carried the whole fantasy.
senses.whyCN: 1920 年 robot 一词诞生之前，automaton 独自承载着全部想象。

senses.title: Blind obedience
senses.definition: someone who obeys orders without question
senses.definitionCN: 不加质疑、唯命是从的人
senses.example: The dictatorship preferred citizens who behaved like automatons.
senses.exampleCN: 独裁政权更喜欢像机器一样顺从的公民。
senses.why: A person who never chooses has surrendered the self-moving power the word names.
senses.whyCN: 从不选择的人，恰恰交出了这个词所说的「自行运动」的能力。

senses.title: In philosophy of mind
senses.definition: a hypothetical being that behaves outwardly human but has no inner experience
senses.definitionCN: 外在行为与人类无异却无内在体验的假想存在
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether we could ever prove another person is not an automaton.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问：我们能否证明他人不是没有内心的自动机？
senses.why: The machine-with-a-face raises the hardest question: where does the mind hide?
senses.whyCN: 顶着人脸的机器提出最艰难的问题：心灵藏在何处？

senses.title: In biology and ethology
senses.definition: an animal or organ acting by fixed mechanisms rather than intelligence
senses.definitionCN: 凭固定机制而非智能行动的动物或器官
senses.example: Descartes treated animal bodies as automatons.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔把动物的身体视为自动机。
senses.why: Descartes split mind from body, leaving animal bodies as self-running machinery.
senses.whyCN: 笛卡尔将心灵与身体分离，动物的身体遂成了自行运转的机械。

intro.en: Automaton comes from Greek automatos, self-moving or acting of one's own will, from autos, self, plus a verb root meaning to think or intend; English borrowed it via Latin in the early seventeenth century.
intro.cn: automaton 出自希腊语 automatos「自行运动、出于己意的」，由 autos「自身」加表「思虑、意图」的动词词根构成；17 世纪初经拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The root *men- meant to think or intend, the same root seen in mind and memory.
items.cn: 词根 *men- 意为「思考、意图」，与 mind、memory 同根。

items.en: autos meant self and a root -matos pointed to intent; automatos meant moving of oneself, unbidden.
items.cn: 希腊语 autos 意为「自身」，-matos 指向意图；automatos 意为自行运动、不召自来。

items.en: Homer used automata of Hephaestus' self-moving golden handmaidens; engineers like Heron built real ones.
items.cn: 荷马用 automata 描写赫菲斯托斯自行运动的黄金侍女；希伦等工程师造出了真实的自动机械。

items.en: Latin adopted automatum for self-moving devices in learned texts.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 automatum 指称学术文本中的自动装置。

items.en: English took automaton in the 1610s, first for self-moving machines and clockwork figures.
items.cn: 17 世纪 10 年代英语收入 automaton，最初指自动机械与发条人偶。

items.en: The 18th-century automaton craze, then computing, gave us both the mocking human sense and the finite automaton.
items.cn: 18 世纪的机关人偶热潮与后来的计算科学，既给了我们讥人的用法，也给了我们有限自动机。

note.en: Group one collects the auto- family and look-alikes; group two collects neighboring machine and obedience words.
note.cn: 第一组收 auto- 词族及形近词；第二组收相邻的机械与盲从词。

entries.definition: self-acting; the adjective of the same Greek automatos.
entries.definitionCN: 自动的；同一希腊词 automatos 的形容词。

entries.definition: the use of self-acting machinery in industry.
entries.definitionCN: 自动化；工业中自动机械的运用。

entries.definition: a self-moving vehicle, from mobile, movable; shares auto- only.
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，出自 mobile「可动的」；仅共享 auto-。

entries.definition: an absolute ruler, from kratos, power; shares auto- but rules people, not gears.
entries.definitionCN: 独裁者，出自 kratos「权力」；共享 auto- 而统辖的是人不是齿轮。

entries.definition: self-shaped, from morphe, form; a mathematics word sharing only the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 自同构的，出自 morphe「形」；数学词，仅共享前缀。

entries.definition: a mechanical agent, from Czech robota, forced labor; coined in 1920.

normalIntro.en: automaton hides three Greek parts: auto for self, mat for intent, on for being.
normalIntro.cn: automaton 藏着三个希腊成分：auto「自身」、mat「意图」、on「存在」。

normal.en: auto (self) + matos (moving of intent): a thing that moves by itself.
normal.cn: auto（自身）+ matos（出于意图的运动）：自己会动的东西。

normal.en: The family: automatic, automation, automate, automaton.
normal.cn: 同族词：automatic、automation、automate、automaton。

normal.en: Plural check: automatons or the Greek automata.
normal.cn: 复数两选一：automatons 或希腊式的 automata。

normal.en: Before robot (1920), automaton was the only word for a mechanical person.
normal.cn: 在 robot（1920）出现前，automaton 是机械人的唯一称呼。

normal.en: Figurative use: an automaton works without thinking, wound up like clockwork.
normal.cn: 比喻用法：automaton 干活不假思索，如上了发条。

abstract.en: Picture a lacquered doll writing a poem as its gears tick.
abstract.cn: 想象一座漆偶在齿轮滴答声中写诗。

abstract.en: The word is a person with the mind taken out, just the motion left.
abstract.cn: 这个词是被抽走心灵、只剩动作的人。

abstract.en: An automaton never asks why; that is the horror and the point.
abstract.cn: automaton 从不问为什么——这正是它的可怖之处，也是此词的要害。

examples.en: The clockmaker's automaton bows to the audience every hour.
examples.cn: 钟表匠造的机关人偶每逢整点向观众鞠躬。

examples.en: He answered the interview questions like an automaton.
examples.cn: 他回答面试问题时像机器人一样刻板。

examples.en: Every finite automaton has states, inputs, and rules.
examples.cn: 每个有限自动机都有状态、输入与规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥透美瞳」——戴上美瞳的奥透像人偶一样，表情僵硬、动作机械

root: 出自希腊语 automatos「自行运动的」（autos「自身」+ 词根 *men-「思虑」的 -matos 形式），荷马已用以描写神匠的自动侍女；经拉丁语 automatum 于 17 世纪初进入英语；与 automatic、automation 同根，与 autocrat（kratos「权力」）仅共享 auto-，词源确凿。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one word from Homer's golden handmaidens to finite-state machines: self-moving devices, mechanical people, blind obedience, and the philosophical puppet that looks human.
sensesIntro.cn: 八义词追溯一个词从荷马的黄金侍女到有限状态机的全程：自行的机械、机械化的人、盲从者，以及形似人类的哲学傀儡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: motion without a mind, a figure that moves as if it chose to.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有心灵的运动，仿佛出于自身选择而动的人偶。

branches.en: THE MACHINE SIDE: clockwork figures, temple doors, and feedback devices.
branches.cn: 机械一面：发条人偶、神庙自动门与反馈装置。

branches.en: THE HUMAN SIDE: workers and citizens who stop choosing.
branches.cn: 人身一面：不再做选择的工人与公民。

branches.en: THE THEORY SIDE: finite automata in mathematics and computing.
branches.cn: 理论一面：数学与计算机中的有限自动机。

branches.en: THE ROBOT SIDE: the older name for what we now call robots.
branches.cn: 机器人一面：如今所谓 robot 的旧称。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHY SIDE: minds questioned in faces and animal bodies.
branches.cn: 哲学一面：被追问心灵的人脸与兽身。

latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 automatos 经拉丁语播下庞大家族：automatic、automation、automate，以及 automaton 本身。

definition_zh: 血统；世系；家系；谱系；一脉相承的传承线
definition_en: the line of descent from an ancestor, or a continuous line of transmission
core_image: 一根从祖辈手里递下来的麻线，线上串着代表每一代人的木珠
scene: 樟木箱里摊着一卷手抄家谱， The elder traces the lineage back to a boatman who landed three centuries earlier.
sceneCN: 这里 lineage 指「一脉相承的血统世系」（第 1 个义项：连续不断的直系传承线）；句意为长者把这条世系一直追溯到三个世纪前靠岸的船夫。图中可辨识物件：手抄家谱、樟木箱、麻线装订、老花镜。

pos.zh: 血统；世系；家系；谱系

senses.title: A continuous line of descent
senses.definition: the unbroken line of descent from a particular ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 自某位祖先起未曾中断的直系传承
senses.example: The family can trace its lineage to a single village on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族能把世系一直追溯到沿海的一座村子。
senses.why: lineage begins as a line drawn through generations, so the core sense is the unbroken thread itself rather than any one person on it.
senses.whyCN: lineage 起初是穿过各代画出的一条线，核心因此是那根不断的线，而不是线上的某个人。

senses.title: A family or stock as a descended group
senses.titleCN: 作为传承群体的家族或族系
senses.definition: a family or stock regarded as a line of related people
senses.definitionCN: 被看作一条相关人群线的家族或族系
senses.example: Two lineages have shared the valley for as long as anyone remembers.
senses.exampleCN: 在所有人记忆所及的年代里，一直有两个族系共用这座山谷。
senses.why: people speak of a lineage when they think of the family as a body that persists through time, not as a list of names.
senses.whyCN: 人们说某个 lineage，是把家族当成一个穿越时间延续的群体，而不是一串名字。

senses.title: A record of ancestry
senses.definition: a written or oral record setting out a line of ancestors
senses.definitionCN: 以书面或口传形式列出一串祖先的记录
senses.example: The monastery kept a lineage of its abbots in the margin of the chronicle.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院在编年史的页边记下了历任院长的传承。
senses.why: once a line is written down, the record itself comes to be called the lineage, as if paper could hold the thread.
senses.whyCN: 一条线一旦被写下来，记录本身也被称作 lineage，仿佛纸能握住那根线。

senses.title: A breeding line in animals or plants
senses.definition: a line of animals or plants maintained through controlled breeding
senses.definitionCN: 通过定向繁育维持下来的动植物品系
senses.example: The seed bank preserves a lineage of drought-tolerant barley.
senses.exampleCN: 种子库保存着一个耐旱大麦品系。
senses.why: breeders think in lines because each generation is selected from the one before, which is the same shape as family descent.
senses.whyCN: 育种者按「线」思考，因为每一代都从上一代选出，这与家族传承形状相同。

senses.title: A line of transmission in texts or ideas
senses.definition: a sequence of copies, versions or ideas derived one from another
senses.definitionCN: 一份份抄本、版本或观念依次由前者派生出的序列
senses.example: Scholars reconstructed the lineage of the three surviving manuscripts.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们重建了三份存世抄本的传承谱系。
senses.why: philology borrowed the family model: a copy descends from an exemplar just as a child descends from a parent.
senses.whyCN: 文献学借用了家族模型：抄本从祖本传下，正如孩子从父母传下。

senses.title: A unilineal descent group in anthropology
senses.titleCN: 人类学中的单系继嗣群
senses.definition: a group whose members trace descent through one parent only
senses.definitionCN: 成员只通过父系或只通过母系追溯血统的群体
senses.example: The lineage owns the terraces and decides who may marry whom.
senses.exampleCN: 这个继嗣群拥有梯田，并决定谁可以与谁通婚。
senses.why: anthropology needed a technical term for a corporate descent group, and lineage already carried the unbroken-line idea.
senses.whyCN: 人类学需要一个术语来指作为法人单位的继嗣群，而 lineage 本就带着「不断的线」这层意思。

senses.title: A pedigree certificate
senses.definition: a document certifying the ancestry of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 证明人或动物血统来源的文书
senses.example: The mare's lineage was printed on a single sheet of stiff paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹母马的血统谱印在一张硬纸上。
senses.why: where ancestry is bought and sold, the paper that proves the line takes the name of the line itself.
senses.whyCN: 在血统可以买卖的地方，证明这条线的纸就沿用了这条线的名字。

senses.title: Any sequence of development
senses.titleCN: 任何前后相续的发展序列
senses.definition: a series of related stages or products following one from another
senses.definitionCN: 一组前后相续的相关阶段或产品
senses.example: The new software has a lineage reaching back to a 1970s drawing program.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新软件的源流可以上溯到 20 世纪 70 年代的一个绘图程序。
senses.why: the family image is so elastic that any series of versions can be given a lineage, even machines.
senses.whyCN: 家族的意象极有弹性，任何一串版本，哪怕是机器，都能被赋予一个 lineage。

intro.en: Lineage comes through Old French from Latin linea 'line, thread', a noun built on linum 'flax'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lineage 经古法语来自拉丁 linea「线、细绳」，该名词建于 linum「亚麻」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Linum meant 'flax', the plant whose fibres were twisted into thread. The deeper origin of the word is not established.
items.cn: linum 意为「亚麻」，这种植物的纤维被捻成线。这个词更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Linea, literally 'a linen thread', came to mean any line, including a line drawn on paper and a boundary.
items.cn: linea 字面是「一根麻线」，后来指任何线，包括纸上画的线与边界。

items.en: Old French ligne kept the sense of a line and also developed the idea of a line of descent.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 保留了「线」的意思，并发展出「血统线」的观念。

items.en: Lignage named the body of people descended from one stock, adding a collective suffix to ligne.
items.cn: lignage 指由同一族系传下的一群人，是在 ligne 之后加集合性后缀构成的。

items.en: English borrowed lineage in the fourteenth century for both the descent line and the family holding it.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 lineage，既指血统线，也指沿这条线延续的家族。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word was extended to breeding lines and to manuscript traditions, where descent is reconstructable but not biological.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个词扩展到育种品系与抄本传统——那里的传承可以重建，却不是生物性的。

note.en: The first group turns on the same Latin thread and is easily mixed up; the second lists other words for ancestry that come from different roots.
note.cn: 第一组共用同一个拉丁「线」词，极易混淆；第二组是同样表示血统、但词根不同的词。

entries.definition: A mark, a row or a connection; the everyday word, with no special claim about ancestors.
entries.definitionCN: 指痕迹、一行或一种联系；是日常用词，对祖先没有专门含义。

entries.definition: Descended in a direct line, as in a lineal heir; an adjective, where lineage is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指直系传承的，如直系继承人；它是形容词，lineage 是名词。

entries.definition: Arranged in or along a line; it describes shape or order and says nothing about descent.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿直线排列的；描述形状或次序，与血统无关。

entries.definition: An obsolete word for the number of lines in a piece of writing, paid by the line; it looks like lineage but means something else.
entries.definitionCN: 一个废弃词，指文稿的行数（按行计酬）；它看起来像 lineage，意思却完全不同。

entries.definition: The whole body of one's forebears rather than the connecting line; it answers who, not how the line runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人全部的先辈，而非那条连接线；它回答「是谁」，而不是「线怎么走」。

entries.definition: A recorded table of ancestors, especially for animals; the document sense of lineage, usually drawn as a chart.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其指动物的血统记录表；相当于 lineage 的文书义，常画成图表。

entries.definition: The relation of being descended from a person or group, viewed as a fact rather than as a continuing thread.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某人或某群体有血缘关系这一事实，被看作事实而非延续的线。

entries.definition: The study of family lines, or a chart of them; it names the discipline, not the family itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指对家族线的研究，或这样的图表；它指这门学问，而非家族本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin word for thread, the words built on it and the collocations that keep it in use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真正表示「线」的拉丁词、由它构成的词，以及让这个词保持活力的搭配。

normal.en: linea 'thread' + -age 'collective body' = the body of people on one thread.
normal.cn: linea「线」+ -age「集合体」= 串在同一根线上的一群人。

normal.en: Latin linum 'flax' also gives linen and line, because thread was made of flax.
normal.cn: 拉丁 linum「亚麻」还给出 linen 与 line，因为线是用亚麻捻成的。

normal.en: The usual phrases are maternal lineage, paternal lineage and trace one's lineage.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是母系世系、父系世系与追溯世系。

normal.en: -age builds a collective noun here, much as it does in baggage and mileage.
normal.cn: 这里的 -age 构成集合名词，作用和 baggage、mileage 里的 -age 一样。

normal.en: In anthropology the word pairs with clan and descent group as a technical unit.
normal.cn: 在人类学里，这个词与「氏族」「世系群」并列为专业单位。

abstract.en: Picture a thread with one wooden bead for every generation, each bead tied by the same knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线上每一代各有一颗木珠，每颗珠子都打着同一个结。

abstract.en: Picture a margin note that repeats a name for four hundred years without changing a letter.
abstract.cn: 想象页边的一行批注，四百年里反复写同一个名字，一个字母都没改。

abstract.en: Picture a single fibre pulled from a page and held up against the light, still unbroken.
abstract.cn: 想象从纸页里抽出一根纤维，对着光举起来，依旧没有断。

examples.en: Her maternal lineage is recorded in a parish register from the 1680s.
examples.cn: 她的母系世系记在 17 世纪 80 年代的一本教区登记簿里。

examples.en: The lineage of these manuscripts can be traced through the scribal notes.
examples.cn: 这些抄本的传承谱系可以靠抄写者留下的批注追溯。

examples.en: A lineage of herders has moved this herd through the same pass each spring.
examples.cn: 一个牧人世系每年春天都赶着这群牲畜走同一道山口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来尼奇」听成「来你继」——一代来、你来继，线不断，就是世系。line 是线，lineage 就是那条代代相传的线。

root: 古法语 lignage，源自 ligne「线」，再上为拉丁 linea「线、麻线」，其基础是 linum「亚麻」。与英语 line、lineal、linear 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all hang on one thread: the descent line, the family on it, the record of it, the breeding and manuscript lines that copy its shape, the clan unit, the certificate and finally any sequence of versions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都挂在一根线上：血统线、线上的家族、对这条线的记载、模仿这条线形状的育种线与抄本线、作为单位的继嗣群、证明文书，最后是任何版本的序列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hemp thread strung with one bead for each generation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根麻线，每一代人串一颗珠。

branches.en: THREAD AND FAMILY: the line itself and the people who occupy it are two views of one object.
branches.cn: 线与家族：线本身与站在线上的两群人是同一物的两种看法。

branches.en: RECORD: once the line is written down, the paper replaces the thread as the thing people consult.
branches.cn: 记载：线一旦写下，纸就取代线，成为人们查阅的对象。

branches.en: BREEDING: selection across generations copies the shape of family descent without any family.
branches.cn: 育种：逐代选育复制了家族传承的形状，却并没有家族。

branches.en: TEXT TRADITION: copies descend from an exemplar, so philology speaks of a manuscript lineage.
branches.cn: 文本传承：抄本自祖本传下，因此文献学说「抄本谱系」。

branches.en: INSTITUTION, PAPER AND PRODUCT: the clan unit, the pedigree sheet and the version series each turn the thread into an object that can be owned or traced.
branches.cn: 制度、纸与产品：继嗣群、血统证明书与版本序列，都把这条线变成可以拥有或追溯的对象。

intro.en: Lineage is a Latin noun for a thread plus a French collective ending, so it can be read as 'the body belonging to one line'.
intro.cn: lineage 是表示「线」的拉丁名词加法语集合后缀，可以读作「属于同一条线的一群」。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea and linum also give line, lineal, linear, linen and align, all through the image of a stretched thread.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 linea 与 linum 还给出 line、lineal、linear、linen、align，全都围绕「拉直的一根线」这一意象。

items.example: The stem supplies the image of a continuous thread.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供「连续不断的线」这一意象。

items.example: The suffix also forms baggage and mileage.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀还构成 baggage 与 mileage。

items.meaning: a mark or row; a connection
items.example: Draw a line from the well to the gate.
items.exampleCN: 从井边到大门画一条线。

items.example: A lineal heir takes before a collateral one.
items.exampleCN: 直系继承人在旁系之前继承。

items.example: The village grew in a linear pattern along the road.
items.exampleCN: 村子沿道路呈线状发展。

items.example: The register was bound in linen.
items.exampleCN: 这本登记簿用亚麻布装订。

items.meaning: to bring into a straight line
items.example: Align the poles with the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 把杆子与山脊对齐。

items.meaning: a body of people on one line
items.example: The lineage holds the lower terraces.
items.exampleCN: 这个世系拥有下面的梯田。

items.meaningCN: 一条条分别来看的世系
items.example: Two lineages share the same spring.
items.exampleCN: 两个世系共用同一处泉水。

definition_zh: 辨明；看出；识别（细微差别）
definition_en: to see or understand something that is faint, hidden or not immediately obvious
core_image: 雾里一盏灯的轮廓慢慢从灰白中浮出来，眼睛要先分开背景才看得见它
scene: 天还没亮，守望的人从雾里辨认出远处灯塔的轮廓。 In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
sceneCN: 这里指从模糊的背景中看出某物的轮廓（第 1 个义项：看清隐约或部分被遮住的东西）；句意：守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。

pos.zh: 辨明；看出；识别
分辨；辨别

senses.title: To perceive something faint or partly hidden
senses.titleCN: 看清隐约或被遮住之物
senses.definition: to make out an object or a sign that is dim, distant or partly concealed
senses.definitionCN: 辨认出模糊、遥远或部分被遮蔽的物体或迹象
senses.example: In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
senses.exampleCN: 守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。
senses.why: The root means to sift, so seeing here is separating an object from the background that hides it.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为筛分，因此这里的看见是把物体从遮蔽它的背景中分开。

senses.title: To tell two similar things apart
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between things that look or sound alike
senses.definitionCN: 认出看起来或听起来相像之物间的差别
senses.example: A trained ear can discern the two instruments in the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 受过训练的耳朵能听出录音中的两件乐器。
senses.why: Sifting is choosing between pieces, and choosing between similar things is the same gesture applied to perception.
senses.whyCN: 筛分就是在碎片之间挑选，在相似之物间作选择是同一动作用在感知上。

senses.title: To judge wisely and see the truth
senses.definition: to understand a situation correctly, especially where others are misled
senses.definitionCN: 正确理解某种处境，尤其在旁人被误导之时
senses.example: She discerned the real reason behind the polite refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 她看出了那道客气拒绝背后的真正原因。
senses.why: Clear sight is used of the mind as well as the eye, so judgement becomes a kind of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 清晰的目光既用于眼睛，也用于心智，因此判断成为一种看见。

senses.title: To notice a pattern or trend
senses.definition: to detect a regularity that is not obvious from a single case
senses.definitionCN: 从单个事例中看不出、但能被察觉的规律性
senses.example: Analysts discern a slow shift in consumer habits.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士看出一股消费者习惯上的缓慢变化。
senses.why: A pattern is hidden in the mass of details, and the verb names the act of separating it out.
senses.whyCN: 模式藏在大量细节里，这个动词命名的是把它分离出来的动作。

senses.title: To read someone's motives
senses.definition: to perceive what a person really intends beneath what is said
senses.definitionCN: 在所说出的话之下察觉某人真正的意图
senses.example: He could discern a little envy in her congratulations.
senses.exampleCN: 他能从她的祝贺中察觉出一点嫉妒。
senses.why: Human motives are faint signals, which is exactly what this verb is built to pick out.
senses.whyCN: 人的动机是微弱的信号，这正是这个动词生来要捕捉的东西。

senses.title: To tell right from wrong
senses.definition: to distinguish morally good conduct from bad without confusing the two
senses.definitionCN: 分清道德上的善与恶，不把两者混淆
senses.example: The old stories teach children to discern right from wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 这些古老的故事教孩子明辨是非。
senses.why: Moral judgement is described as seeing clearly, since the failure involved is a failure to distinguish.
senses.whyCN: 道德判断被描述成看得清楚，因为这里的失误就是分辨不清。

senses.title: To distinguish slight sensory differences
senses.definition: to notice small differences in taste, smell, colour or texture
senses.definitionCN: 察觉味道、气味、颜色或质地上的细微差异
senses.example: Few tasters can discern the difference between the two teas.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有品茶者能辨出这两种茶的差别。
senses.why: The senses are the original training ground for sifting, and fine tasting is its most literal survival.
senses.whyCN: 感官本是筛分能力最初的训练场，精细品鉴是它最字面的留存。

senses.title: To find structure in data or noise
senses.titleCN: 从数据或噪声中找出结构
senses.definition: to detect a real signal inside a mass of random or confusing information
senses.definitionCN: 在一大堆随机或混乱的信息中察觉真实的信号
senses.example: The software discerns a weak signal beneath the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件在噪声之下辨出一个微弱信号。
senses.why: Modern research is a new field for an old act: separating a signal from everything that covers it.
senses.whyCN: 现代研究给古老动作提供了新场地：把信号从覆盖它的一切中分离出来。

intro.en: Discern comes from a Latin verb meaning to separate and so to distinguish, built from a prefix of separation and a verb for sifting. English took it through French in the fourteenth century, and its noun became the ordinary word for judgement.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示分开、因而表示辨别的拉丁动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示筛分的动词构成。英语在十四世纪经法语借入，其名词后来成为表示判断力的常用词。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from that came the sense of distinguishing one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为筛分、分开，由此产生把一物与另一物区别开来的含义。

items.en: The prefix meant apart, so the compound pictured taking one thing out of a mixture.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开，因此复合词描绘的是把某物从混合物中取出来。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to separate, to distinguish and to perceive clearly.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为分开、区别、看清。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English in the fourteenth century, where it settled in both sight and judgement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个动词带到英语，它在视觉与判断两方面都站稳了脚。

items.en: The English noun became the fixed word for good judgement, especially in moral and practical matters.
items.cn: 英语名词成为表示良好判断力的固定说法，尤其用于道德与实际事务。

items.en: Statistics and signal processing gave the old act of sifting a new object: structure hidden in noise.
items.cn: 统计学与信号处理给古老的筛分动作配上新对象：藏在噪声里的结构。

note.en: The first group shares the sifting root or its English descendants; the second group names nearby acts of seeing and distinguishing. Discern is an act of perception that separates something faint from its background, while deduce is a chain of steps from premises to a conclusion.
note.cn: 第一组共享筛分词根或其英语后裔；第二组是相邻的看见与区分动作。本词是从背景中分离出模糊之物的感知动作，推演类词则是从前提走向结论的步骤链。

entries.definition: The capacity for fine judgement, especially about people and values.
entries.definitionCN: 精细判断的能力，尤其关于人与价值。

entries.definition: Showing good judgement, as in a discerning reader.
entries.definitionCN: 显示良好判断力的，如有眼力的读者。

entries.definition: Careful about what one says; it comes from the same Latin participle but lost the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 说话谨慎；出自同一个拉丁分词，却丢掉了「看见」之义。

entries.definition: Separate and distinct, which is the literal sense of the shared participle.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立的，正是那个共享分词的字面义。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses; it is the general word.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官觉察某物；是泛称。

entries.definition: To mark a difference between things; the emphasis is on the difference, not the faintness.
entries.definitionCN: 标出事物间的差别；强调差别，而非微弱。

entries.definition: To discover something hidden or hard to notice, often by instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或难以察觉之物，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To draw fine distinctions; also used for unfair treatment, a sense this word avoids.
entries.definitionCN: 作精细区分；也用于不公平对待，而本词避开后一义。

entries.definition: To manage to see or hear something with difficulty; the everyday phrase for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地看清或听清；是第一个义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the sifting root, the real family and the fixed phrases of perception and judgement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用筛分词根、真实同族词，以及感知与判断方面的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root means to sift, so the verb means to separate one thing from everything around it.
normal.cn: 词根意为筛分，动词就是把某物从周围一切中分出来。

normal.en: The family runs discernment, discerning, discernible and indiscernible.
normal.cn: 同族词有辨别力、有眼力的、可辨认的与难以辨认的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: discern a difference, discern the truth, barely discern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：辨出差别、辨明真相、勉强辨认。

normal.en: The eye and the mind share the verb, which is why judgement is described as clear sight.
normal.cn: 眼睛与心智共用这个动词，因此判断被描述成清晰的看见。

normal.en: Two look-alike adjectives came from the same participle: one means tactful, one means separate.
normal.cn: 两个形近形容词出自同一分词：一个表示谨慎，一个表示分离。

abstract.en: Picture a shape slowly separating itself from a grey wall of fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一个形状慢慢从灰色的雾墙中分离出来。

abstract.en: Picture two nearly identical threads that only a careful hand can tell apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两根几乎一样的线，只有细心的手能分开。

abstract.en: Picture a single clear note heard under the noise of a whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的喧闹下，一个清亮的音符被听见。

examples.en: It was hard to discern anything in the dark room.
examples.cn: 在漆黑的房间里很难看清任何东西。

examples.en: She discerned a note of worry beneath his calm voice.
examples.cn: 她从他平静的声音里辨出一丝担忧。

examples.en: The study discerns no clear trend in the data.
examples.cn: 这项研究在数据中看不出明确的趋势。

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把微弱之物从背景中分离出来：轮廓、差别、真相、模式、动机、是非、味道与噪声中的信号。

branches.en: THE SENSES: a dim outline made out, and two similar things told apart.
branches.cn: 感官：看清模糊轮廓，并分辨两个相似之物。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: the real cause understood, and right separated from wrong.
branches.cn: 判断：理解真正原因，并把是非分开。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: a regularity extracted from a mass of detail.
branches.cn: 模式：从大量细节中抽出的规律。

branches.en: THE PERSON: an intention read beneath what is said.
branches.cn: 人：从言语之下读出的意图。

branches.en: THE FINE DIFFERENCE: a slight taste distinguished, and a weak signal found in noise.
branches.cn: 细微差别：辨出细微味道，以及在噪声中找到微弱信号。

senses.title: A part that makes up a whole
senses.titleCN: 组成部分：构成整体的一部分
senses.definition: one of the separate parts that together form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成一个整体的各个部分之一
senses.example: Each constituent of the machine can be replaced separately.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器的每个组成部分都可以单独更换。
senses.why: Constituent comes from Latin constituens, the present participle of constituere 'to set up, establish'. A constituent is literally 'a thing set into' a larger whole: it has been placed in the structure and helps hold it up.
senses.whyCN: constituent 来自拉丁语 constituens，即 constituere“设立、建立”的现在分词。组成部分字面上就是“被安置进”更大整体中的东西：它被放进结构里，并帮助撑起结构。

senses.title: A substance that forms part of a mixture
senses.titleCN: 物质成分：混合物中的某种成分
senses.definition: a substance that is one of the materials making up a mixture or structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成混合物或结构的一种材料
senses.example: Calcium is a key constituent of bone.
senses.exampleCN: 钙是骨骼的一种关键成分。
senses.why: The same 'set into' image applies to matter: a chemical constituent has been placed into the mixture and is part of its make-up. The -ent form names the thing that has been constituted into the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“被安置进去”的形象也适用于物质：化学成分被放进混合物，成为其组成的一部分。-ent 形式命名那个被构成进整体的东西。

senses.title: Constituent assembly: a body that sets up a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪会议：设立国家的机构
senses.definition: a specially elected assembly whose task is to draw up a constitution
senses.definitionCN: 为起草宪法而专门选出的代表会议
senses.example: The constituent assembly drafted the new republic's charter.
senses.exampleCN: 制宪会议起草了新共和国的宪章。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the verb's active force: a constituent assembly is an assembly that constitutes, that sets up the state's fundamental order. Here the word describes the setting-up act itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了动词的主动力量：constituent assembly 就是“进行构成”的会议，它设立国家的基本秩序。这里这个词描述的是“设立”这一行为本身。

senses.title: Constituent country: a unit inside a union
senses.titleCN: 构成国：联合体内的组成单位
senses.definition: a country or state that forms part of a larger political union, such as the United Kingdom
senses.definitionCN: 构成更大政治联合体（如英国）的一部分的国家或地区
senses.example: Scotland is a constituent country of the United Kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰是英国的构成国。
senses.why: A constituent country is a country that helps constitute a larger state. The same participle logic applies: it is a unit set into the union. Note that the voting district itself is a constituency, not a constituent.
senses.whyCN: 构成国是帮助构成更大国家的国家。同样的分词逻辑：它是被安置进联合体的单位。注意：选区本身是 constituency，而不是 constituent。

senses.title: A grammatical unit in a sentence
senses.titleCN: 语法成分：句子中的结构单位
senses.definition: a word or group of words that functions as a single unit within a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在句子中作为一个单位起作用的词或词组
senses.example: In 'the old bridge', the whole phrase is a constituent of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 在 the old bridge 中，整个短语是句子的一个成分。
senses.why: Modern linguistics borrowed the word for structure: a constituent is a piece 'set into' a larger sentence and can be moved or replaced as a unit. The Latin 'standing in a structure' sense becomes grammatical analysis.
senses.whyCN: 现代语言学借这个词来描述结构：语法成分是“被安置进”更大句子的片段，可以作为一个单位移动或替换。拉丁语“站在结构中”的意思变成了语法分析。

senses.title: An essential element of a concept or situation
senses.titleCN: 构成要素：使事物成立的关键元素
senses.definition: an element that is necessary for something to exist or be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 某事物存在或成为自身所必需的元素
senses.example: Trust is a constituent element of a healthy partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是健康合作关系的一个构成要素。
senses.why: The word moves from physical parts to abstract ones. A constituent element is still something 'set into' the whole, but now the whole is a relationship or idea rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物质部分转向抽象部分。构成要素仍然是“被安置进”整体的东西，只是这个整体现在是关系或观念，而不是物体。

senses.title: A voter in a district
senses.titleCN: 选民：选区中有投票权的人
senses.definition: a person who lives in an electoral district and has the right to vote there
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一选区并有投票权的人
senses.example: The senator met with constituents at the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参议员在市政厅会见选民。
senses.why: In political usage the person 'constitutes' the electorate: voters set up the representative body. The noun shifted from 'one who constitutes' to 'one who is represented', a concrete political role.
senses.whyCN: 在政治用法中，个人“构成”选民群体：选民设立了代议机构。名词从“构成者”转为“被代表者”，成为一个具体的政治角色。

senses.title: Constituent power: the authority to found a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪权：创立国家的权力
senses.definition: the ultimate authority of a people to establish or change its constitution
senses.definitionCN: 人民设立或改变其宪法的终极权力
senses.example: The court debated whether the people hold constituent power.
senses.exampleCN: 法院讨论了人民是否拥有制宪权。
senses.why: Here the adjective names the power that constitutes: the capacity to set up the legal order itself. It is the most abstract extension of constituere 'establish', applied to the founding act rather than to a part.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词命名“进行构成”的权力：设立法律秩序本身的能力。这是 constituere“建立”最抽象的延伸，作用于创立行为而非某个部分。

senses.title: Constituent structure: the arrangement of parts
senses.titleCN: 成分结构：各部分的层级组织
senses.definition: the hierarchical arrangement of parts within a sentence or system
senses.definitionCN: 句子或系统内部各部分的层级排列方式
senses.example: The tree diagram shows the constituent structure of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 树形图展示了这个句子的成分结构。
senses.why: Structure names the way constituents are set together. The word keeps its compositional sense but now describes the whole arrangement rather than any single part; -ent still marks the unit that has been set in.
senses.whyCN: 结构命名各成分被放在一起的方式。这个词保留组合义，但现在描述整体排列而非单个部分；-ent 仍标记那个被安置进去的单位。

intro.en: Constituent is a Latin present participle in -ent, from constituere 'set up, establish'. The base verb splits into con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: constituent 是带 -ent 的拉丁语现在分词，来自 constituere“设立、建立”。基础动词拆为 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Constituere means 'to set up, establish, appoint, constitute'. It is a compound of con- 'together' and statuere 'to place, set, fix'.
items.cn: constituere 意为“设立、建立、任命、构成”。它由 con-“一起”和 statuere“放置、设立、固定”复合而成。

items.en: Its present participle is constituens, stem constituent-, 'setting up; that which sets up'. This is the exact form English borrows, so the word arrives already carrying the active idea of putting something in place.
items.cn: 它的现在分词是 constituens，词干 constituent-，意为“正在设立的；设立者”。英语借用的正是这一形式，因此这个词一进入英语就带着“把某物安放到位”的主动含义。

items.en: The -ent suffix (Latin -ent-) makes an adjective or noun from the participle. As an adjective, constituent means 'forming part of'; as a noun, 'the thing that constitutes' or 'one who constitutes'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ent（拉丁语 -ent-）把分词变成形容词或名词。作形容词时 constituent 意为“构成部分的”；作名词时意为“构成之物”或“构成者”。

items.en: English adopts constituent in the 16c. as both adjective and noun, first in the general sense 'forming part of a whole'. The political senses grow from the idea of parts that set up a larger body.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪引入 constituent，形容词与名词并用，最初是一般义“构成整体的一部分”。政治义从“设立更大机构的部分”这一观念生长出来。

items.en: By the 18c. a constituent is 'a person who has the right to elect a representative'. The voter is the person who constitutes the representative body, so the noun moves from maker to member of the electorate.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，constituent 指“有权选举代表的人”。选民是构成代议机构的人，因此名词从“构成者”转为“选民群体的一员”。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense (a constituent of a mixture), the political senses (constituent assembly, constituent power, voter), and the 20c. linguistic sense of a syntactic unit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物质义（混合物的成分）、政治义（制宪会议、制宪权、选民），以及 20 世纪语言学的句法单位义。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that are often confused with constituent; the second holds nouns that also name a part of a whole.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 constituent 混淆的同族词；第二组是同样表示“整体的一部分”的名词。

entries.definition: a voting district or the voters in it. It is the place or group, while a constituent is one voter.
entries.definitionCN: 选区或该区选民。它是地区或群体，而 constituent 是其中一位选民。

entries.definition: to form or make up something; to establish. It is the verb behind constituent.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物；设立。它是 constituent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the fundamental law of a state, or the make-up of a body. It is the -tion noun from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 国家的根本法，或身体的构成。它是同一动词加 -tion 的名词。

entries.definition: a part of a larger machine or system. It is close to constituent but more common in technical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 较大机器或系统的一部分。它与 constituent 接近，但更常用于技术语境。

entries.definition: one of the basic parts of something. It is broader and can be abstract or chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的基本部分之一。它更宽泛，可指抽象要素或化学元素。

entries.definition: one of the foods or substances combined to make something. It is mostly used for cooking and mixtures.
entries.definitionCN: 组合成某物的食材或物质之一。它多用于烹饪和混合物。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. It is the everyday word that constituent formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分。它是 constituent 所正式化的日常词。

entries.definition: one element that contributes to a result. It is about influence rather than physical make-up.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的一个要素。它讲的是影响，而不是物理构成。

normalIntro.en: These links use the real constituere family, the real -ent participle ending, and real political collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联系使用真实的 constituere 词族、真实的分词后缀 -ent，以及真实政治搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + statuere 'set' + -ent 'the one doing': a constituent is a thing set into the whole.
normal.cn: con-“一起” + statuere“放置” + -ent“做此事者”：constituent 就是被安置进整体的东西。

normal.en: Keep the family apart: constitute is the verb, constituent is a part or voter, constitution is the fundamental law, constituency is the district.
normal.cn: 分清词族：constitute 是动词，constituent 是部分或选民，constitution 是根本法，constituency 是选区。

normal.en: The political phrases are fixed: constituent assembly, constituent power, constituent country.
normal.cn: 政治短语是固定的：constituent assembly、constituent power、constituent country。

normal.en: A constituent is one voter; all the voters together form a constituency. One letter changes the unit.
normal.cn: 一位选民是 constituent；全体选民构成 constituency。一个字母之差，单位就变了。

normal.en: In grammar, a constituent is any word or phrase that can stand as a unit inside a larger sentence.
normal.cn: 在语法中，成分是任何能在更大句子中作为一个单位站立的词或短语。

abstract.en: Picture a wall: each brick is set into it and helps hold it up. That brick is a constituent; the wall is the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙：每块砖都被砌进去，并帮助撑住墙。那块砖就是 constituent，墙则是整体。

abstract.en: The word always implies placement. A constituent is not just nearby; it has been put in and is part of the structure.
abstract.cn: 这个词总含有“被安放”的意味。组成部分不是仅仅在旁边，而是被放进去、成为结构的一部分。

abstract.en: The voter sense keeps the same logic: voters are the pieces that set up the representative body.
abstract.cn: 选民义保留同一逻辑：选民是设立代议机构的那些“部件”。

examples.en: Protein is a major constituent of every living cell.
examples.cn: 蛋白质是每个活细胞的主要成分。

examples.en: The constituent assembly began drafting the constitution in 1787.
examples.cn: 制宪会议于 1787 年开始起草宪法。

examples.en: The representative holds a weekly meeting with her constituents.
examples.cn: 这位代表每周与她的选民会面。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯斯提球恩特”——肯斯提把球摁特进墙里，每块砖都是组成部分 → constituent 成分

root: 拉丁 constituere“设立、放置”（con- 一起 + statuere 放置）+ -ent（分词后缀）：被安置进整体、构成本身的那一部分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of constituent all come from 'something set into a whole'. The whole may be a machine, a mixture, a state, a sentence, a relationship, or an electorate.
sensesIntro.cn: constituent 的九个义项都来自“被安置进整体的东西”。这个整体可以是机器、混合物、国家、句子、关系或选民群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brick set into a wall, each brick helping to hold the wall up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块块砖被砌进同一面墙，每块砖都帮助撑住墙。

branches.en: PART AND ELEMENT: a concrete part of a whole, and an essential element of an idea or situation.
branches.cn: 部分与要素：整体的具体部分，以及观念或情境中不可缺少的元素。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND STRUCTURE: a substance inside a mixture, and the arrangement of all the parts.
branches.cn: 物质与结构：混合物中的物质成分，以及所有部分的排列方式。

branches.en: FOUNDING: an assembly that sets up a state, and the ultimate power to do so.
branches.cn: 创立：设立国家的会议，以及这样做的终极权力。

branches.en: POLITICAL MEMBERSHIP: a unit inside a union, and a voter inside a district.
branches.cn: 政治成员：联合体内部的组成单位，以及选区内部的选民。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word or phrase functioning as one structural unit.
branches.cn: 语法：作为一个结构单位起作用的词或短语。

intro.en: Constituent is built from the Latin participle constituens. English adds no new prefix here; the -ent ending is the same suffix that makes adjectives such as consistent and different.
intro.cn: constituent 由拉丁语分词 constituens 构成。英语在这里没有再加新前缀；-ent 就是构成 consistent、different 等形容词的同一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is constituere, from con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Constituens is its present participle, and the -ent- stem is what English borrows.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 constituere，来自 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。constituens 是它的现在分词，英语借用的就是 -ent- 词干。

items.meaning: to form, make up, or establish
items.meaningCN: 构成；设立（con- 表示“一起”）
items.example: Twelve members constitute the committee.
items.exampleCN: 十二名成员构成了这个委员会。

items.meaning: a part that makes up a whole
items.meaningCN: 组成部分；成分（-ent 分词后缀）
items.example: Water is a constituent of every cell.
items.exampleCN: 水是每个细胞的成分。

items.meaning: the fundamental law or make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 宪法；体质；构成（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The country adopted a new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家通过了新宪法。

items.meaningCN: 宪法的；合宪的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The court reviewed the constitutional question.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了这个宪法问题。

items.meaning: a voting district or its voters
items.meaningCN: 选区；选民群体（-cy 构成名词）
items.example: The candidate visited every town in the constituency.
items.exampleCN: 候选人走访了选区的每个城镇。

items.meaning: more than one part or voter
items.meaningCN: 多个组成部分或选民（复数后缀）
items.example: The medicine contains several active constituents.
items.exampleCN: 这种药含有几种活性成分。

items.meaning: formed or established in the past
items.meaningCN: 构成了；设立了（过去式／过去分词）
items.example: The tribunal was constituted in 1998.
items.exampleCN: 该法庭于 1998 年设立。

items.example: The fields constituting the park are protected.
items.exampleCN: 构成公园的那些田地受到保护。

items.meaning: essential to the make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 构成的；本质性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is a constitutive part of human culture.
items.exampleCN: 语言是人类文化的构成性部分。

latinEntries.meaning: setting up; that which sets up

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示具有某种性质或执行某动作的

definition_zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度
definition_en: the speed of something in a given direction, or the rate at which something moves or changes
core_image: 一支箭离弦后，箭头旁画着一条带箭头的直线，线上标着等距刻度
scene: 实验台上，小车沿倾斜导轨滑下，两道光门依次亮起，计时器记下通过的时刻。 The sensor measured the cart's velocity as it passed each gate.
sceneCN: 这里 velocity 指物体在某一方向上的运动快慢（第 1 个义项：带方向的速度矢量）；句意：传感器测出小车经过每道光门时的速度。图中可辨识物件：倾斜导轨、小车、光门、计时器。

pos.zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度

senses.title: Speed with a direction
senses.definition: the rate at which an object changes position, measured as distance divided by time and stated with a direction
senses.definitionCN: 物体位置改变的速率，以距离除以时间计量，并标明方向
senses.example: Velocity differs from speed in that it must include a direction.
senses.exampleCN: 速度与速率的不同在于，速度必须包含方向。
senses.why: Physicists needed a word for speed tied to a direction, and Latin velocitas supplied the plain word for swiftness.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要一个词来表示与方向绑定的快慢，拉丁 velocitas 正好提供了「迅速」这个朴素的词。

senses.title: Swiftness in everyday speech
senses.definition: the speed at which something moves, without the technical idea of direction
senses.definitionCN: 某物移动的快慢，不带方向这一技术含义
senses.example: The train gathered velocity as it left the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 火车驶出山谷时越来越快。
senses.why: Outside the laboratory the direction is often left out, so velocity simply means high speed.
senses.whyCN: 出了实验室，方向常被略去，velocity 就单纯指「快」。

senses.title: Rate of a change or process
senses.definition: the rate at which a process or quantity changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 某一过程或数量随时间变化的快慢
senses.example: The velocity of the reaction fell as the mixture cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 混合物冷却后，反应速率下降了。
senses.why: Velocity measures how fast a distance grows; any quantity that grows at a steady rate can take the same word.
senses.whyCN: velocity 衡量距离增长得多快；任何按稳定速率增长的量，都能用同一个词。

senses.title: The circulation rate of money
senses.definition: the average number of times money changes hands in an economy over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内货币在经济中平均转手的次数
senses.example: A higher velocity of money can raise prices without more cash.
senses.exampleCN: 货币流通速度提高，不必增加现金也能推高物价。
senses.why: Economists treat money as a body in motion: the faster it passes from hand to hand, the higher its velocity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把钱看作在运动的东西：它转手越快，速度就越高。

senses.title: The speed of a projectile
senses.definition: the speed of a bullet, shell or thrown object at a stated point in its flight
senses.definitionCN: 子弹、炮弹或抛射物在飞行中某一指定点的速度
senses.example: The muzzle velocity of the rifle was recorded for every batch.
senses.exampleCN: 每一批步枪的出膛速度都有记录。
senses.why: Gunners measured how fast a shot leaves the barrel and called that measured speed its velocity.
senses.whyCN: 炮手测量弹丸离膛多快，并把这一测得的速度称作它的 velocity。

senses.title: The rate of rotation
senses.definition: the rate at which an object turns about an axis, usually given in radians per second
senses.definitionCN: 物体绕轴旋转的速率，通常以每秒弧度表示
senses.example: The wheel's angular velocity doubled when the load was removed.
senses.exampleCN: 卸去负载后，轮子的角速度加倍。
senses.why: Turning is motion around an axis, so the same measuring word was applied to angles rather than to straight distance.
senses.whyCN: 转动是绕轴的运动，于是同一个测量词被用到角度上，而不是直线距离上。

senses.title: The steady speed of a falling body
senses.definition: the constant speed reached when the force of gravity is balanced by air resistance
senses.definitionCN: 重力与空气阻力相平衡时达到的恒定速度
senses.example: A falling raindrop reaches terminal velocity within a few metres.
senses.exampleCN: 雨滴落下几米就达到收尾速度。
senses.why: When a falling body stops speeding up, its velocity has become steady, and the phrase names that end point.
senses.whyCN: 当落体不再加速，它的速度就稳定了，这个说法指的就是那个终点。

senses.title: The speed of light
senses.definition: the constant speed at which light travels in a vacuum, about three hundred million metres per second
senses.definitionCN: 光在真空中传播的恒定速度，约为每秒三亿米
senses.example: The velocity of light sets the limit for every signal we send.
senses.exampleCN: 光速为我们发出的每一个信号设定了上限。
senses.why: The speed of light became the fixed reference speed of physics, so it is called the velocity of light.
senses.whyCN: 光速成了物理学的固定参考速度，因此被称为「光的 velocity」。

intro.en: Velocity comes from Latin velocitas, swiftness, built on velox 'swift'. It entered English in the seventeenth century as mechanics began to measure motion, but the deeper origin of velox is unsettled.
intro.cn: velocity 来自拉丁 velocitas「迅速」，由 velox「快」构成。它在十七世纪随力学开始定量测量运动而进入英语，但 velox 的更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Velox meant swift or quick; it described horses, runners and anything that moves fast.
items.cn: velox 意为迅捷、快；可形容马、奔跑者以及任何动得快的东西。

items.en: Velocitas, built on velox, was the noun for swiftness, used of bodies and of the passing of time.
items.cn: velocitas 由 velox 构成，是表示「迅速」的名词，用于物体，也用于时间的流逝。

items.en: English borrowed velocity in the seventeenth century, when mechanics began to measure motion numerically.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 velocity，当时力学开始用数字测量运动。

items.en: The vector sense, speed tied to a direction, became standard in physics teaching in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 把快慢与方向绑定的矢量义，在十九世纪的物理教学中成为标准。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of velox is not established. A link with vehere 'to carry' has been suggested but not demonstrated, so no Indo-European root should be asserted.
items.cn: 来源不确定：velox 的更深来源未得到确认。有人提出它与 vehere「运送」有关，但未获证实，因此不应断言某个印欧词根。

items.en: The first dates for the technical and economic senses are approximate; the word itself is well recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 技术义与经济义的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十七世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for swift or merely rhymes with velocity; the second group separates velocity from speed, rate and momentum.
note.cn: 第一组或共享那个表示「快」的拉丁词，或只是与 velocity 音近；第二组把 velocity 与 speed、rate、momentum 区分开。

entries.definition: A rare adjective from Latin velox, meaning swift; it describes the quality, not a measured quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 velox 而来的罕用形容词，意为迅疾；描述性质，不是可测的量。

entries.definition: An early pedal or hand-cranked vehicle; from Latin velox plus pes 'foot', so it means swift-footed.
entries.definitionCN: 早期的脚踏或手摇车辆；由拉丁 velox 加 pes「脚」构成，意为「快脚」。

entries.definition: A track for cycle racing; its first part goes back through French vélo to velocipede, and so to velox.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车赛道；前半部分经法语 vélo 上溯到 velocipede，再上溯到 velox。

entries.definition: From Latin verax 'truthful', built on verus 'true'; it looks like velocity but has nothing to do with speed.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 verax「诚实的」，由 verus「真」构成；形似 velocity，却与速度无关。

entries.definition: From Latin vorax 'greedy', built on vorare 'to devour'; another word in -acity that only sounds like velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vorax「贪食的」，由 vorare「吞食」构成；又一个只在读音上像 velocity 的词。

entries.definition: The distance covered per unit time without direction; velocity adds direction and is a vector.
entries.definitionCN: 单位时间内走过的距离，不带方向；velocity 加上方向，是矢量。

entries.definition: The rate of movement, often of walking or of a repeated action; it is less technical than velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢，常指走路或重复动作的节奏；不如 velocity 技术化。

entries.definition: A measure of change per unit of time; velocity is a particular rate applied to position.
entries.definitionCN: 单位时间内的变化量；velocity 是这一量用在位置上的特例。

entries.definition: Mass multiplied by velocity; it measures the push a moving body can deliver, not its speed alone.
entries.definitionCN: 质量乘以速度；衡量运动物体能给出的推力，不只是快慢。

entries.definition: The rate at which velocity itself changes; it is the slope of a velocity graph, not the speed.
entries.definitionCN: 速度本身变化的快慢；是速度图线的斜率，不是速度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Velox is Latin for swift, and velocitas is swiftness.
normal.cn: velox 是拉丁语「快」，velocitas 就是「迅速」。

normal.en: The family runs velocity, velocities, velocious, velocimeter, velocimetry.
normal.cn: 同族词有 velocity、velocities、velocious、velocimeter、velocimetry。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: average velocity, angular velocity, terminal velocity, velocity of money.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：平均速度、角速度、收尾速度、货币流通速度。

normal.en: Physics keeps the difference: velocity is a vector, speed is its size.
normal.cn: 物理守住这个区别：velocity 是矢量，speed 是它的大小。

normal.en: Guns and economics both use it: muzzle velocity for a shot, velocity of money for spending.
normal.cn: 枪炮与经济学都用它：弹丸讲出膛速度，花钱讲货币流通速度。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow already in the air, a straight line drawn beside it with even ticks.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭已在空中，旁边画着一条带均匀刻度的直线。

abstract.en: Picture a needle on a dial climbing past every mark at once.
abstract.cn: 想象表盘上的指针一口气冲过所有刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a coin passing from hand to hand so fast it never rests.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币在人手间飞快传递，从不停下。

examples.en: The probe's velocity was calculated from two radar readings.
examples.cn: 探测器的速度由两次雷达读数算出。

examples.en: The cyclist held a steady velocity along the flat road.
examples.cn: 骑车人在平路上保持着稳定的速度。

examples.en: Economists watch the velocity of money as a sign of spending.
examples.cn: 经济学家把货币流通速度看作消费的迹象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ve（微）+ lo（乐）+ city（城市）」——一路乐着穿过城市，越走越快；velocity 速度

root: 拉丁 velox「快」→ 拉丁 velocitas「迅速」→ 英语 velocity；velox 的更深来源不确定，与 vehere「运送」的联系仅为假说，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one arrow: it carries a direction, flies fast in plain speech, measures any process, times the circulation of money, leaves a barrel, turns a wheel, settles into a fall, and finally limits every signal as the speed of light.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一支箭展开：它带着方向、在日常话里飞快、可量任何过程、计货币的流通、离膛而出、带动车轮旋转、在坠落中稳定下来，最后作为光速为一切信号设限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow leaves the bow, and a straight line with even ticks is drawn beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭离弦而出，旁边画着一条带均匀刻度的直线。

branches.en: THE VECTOR: distance per time with a direction attached is the measuring core of the word.
branches.cn: 矢量：距离除以时间并附上方向，是这个词的测量核心。

branches.en: SPEED AND RATE: everyday speech drops the direction, and any growing quantity can borrow the same measure.
branches.cn: 快慢与速率：日常说话略去方向，任何增长的量也能借用同一测量。

branches.en: MONEY IN MOTION: economists count how fast cash passes from hand to hand.
branches.cn: 运动的钱：经济学家计算现金转手有多快。

branches.en: MEASURED MOTION: a shot, a spinning wheel and a falling drop are each given a velocity at a chosen point.
branches.cn: 被测量的运动：弹丸、转轮与落滴，各在选定的一点上给出速度。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: light travels at a fixed speed that no signal can exceed.
branches.cn: 上限：光以固定速度传播，任何信号都无法超过。

intro.en: Velocity is a Latin noun of swiftness, and its root builds a small family of measuring words in English.
intro.cn: velocity 是一个表示「迅速」的拉丁名词，它的词根在英语里构成一小族与测量有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin velox 'swift' gives velocitas and velocity, and also velocipede, velodrome and the rare velocious; the ending -ity forms nouns of quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 velox「快」衍生 velocitas 与 velocity，也衍生 velocipede、velodrome 与罕用的 velocious；后缀 -ity 构成表性质的名词。

items.example: The adjective supplies the idea of speed to the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为整个词族提供「快」的意思。

items.example: The Latin noun names the quality of being swift.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指「快」这一性质。

items.example: The sensor measured the cart's velocity.
items.exampleCN: 传感器测出了小车的速度。

items.example: The two velocities were averaged.
items.exampleCN: 两个速度值被取了平均。

items.example: A velocious current swept the boat downstream.
items.exampleCN: 一股迅疾的水流把小船冲向下游。

items.example: The velocimeter was fixed to the rail.
items.exampleCN: 速度计固定在导轨上。

items.example: Laser velocimetry mapped the flow.
items.exampleCN: 激光测速法绘出了流场。

items.example: The velodrome hosted the final sprint.
items.exampleCN: 自行车赛场承办了最后的冲刺赛。

items.meaningCN: 构成表性质名词的后缀
items.example: The ending turns an adjective of speed into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示快的形容词变成名词。

definition_zh: 客观地；不带个人偏见地；依据事实地；从外部看地
definition_en: in a way based on observable facts rather than personal feelings, opinions, or interests
core_image: 一台摄像机架在房间角落，不参与对话，只把每个人说的话原样录下来。
scene: 两位评审先各自独立打分，再对照结果，避免互相影响。 Each reviewer scored the papers objectively before comparing notes.
sceneCN: 这里 objectively 是“不带个人偏见地、依据可观察事实地”（第 1 个义项）；句意：每位评审在对照之前都客观地给论文打分。

pos.zh: 客观地；不带个人偏见地；依据事实地；从外部看地

senses.title: Without personal bias
senses.titleCN: 不带偏见：把自己的好恶放到一边
senses.definition: in a manner free from personal preference, prejudice, or interest
senses.definitionCN: 不带个人偏好、成见或利益的方式
senses.example: The reviewer tried to judge the manuscript objectively, though she disliked its topic.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管不喜欢这个题目，评审仍努力客观地评判稿件。
senses.why: Objectivity begins with separating the observer's feelings from the judgement; the adverb says the separation was attempted.
senses.whyCN: 客观始于把观察者的感受与判断分开；这个副词表示这种分离被付诸实践。

senses.title: On the evidence available
senses.titleCN: 依据事实：让证据先说话
senses.definition: by relying on evidence that others can examine, rather than on private impressions
senses.definitionCN: 依据他人也能查验的证据，而非私人印象
senses.example: The damage was assessed objectively from photographs and measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 损失是依据照片与测量数据客观评估的。
senses.why: A judgement is objective when it can be checked: the evidence stands outside the judge and can be produced again for someone else.
senses.whyCN: 当判断可以被复核时，它就是客观的：证据在判断者之外，可以再拿出来给别人看。

senses.title: Open to measurement
senses.titleCN: 可客观测量：尺子和仪器说了算
senses.definition: in a way that can be measured or counted by instruments independent of the observer
senses.definitionCN: 可由独立于观察者的仪器测量或计数的方式
senses.example: Improvement was measured objectively as the number of errors per page.
senses.exampleCN: 进步以每页错误数这一指标被客观测量。
senses.why: Measurement turns a claim into a number that another lab can repeat; the adverb marks that the number, not the impression, carries the argument.
senses.whyCN: 测量把主张变成另一个实验室也能复现的数字；这个副词标明是数字而非印象在支撑论证。

senses.title: True regardless of opinion
senses.titleCN: 客观上成立：谁怎么看都改变不了
senses.definition: in a way that holds independently of what anyone believes or feels
senses.definitionCN: 不以任何人的信念或感受为转移地成立
senses.example: The task was objectively harder, even if the volunteers enjoyed it more.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务客观上更难，即使志愿者更喜欢它。
senses.why: This sense asserts independence from belief: the fact would remain what it is even if every observer changed their mind.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项主张独立于信念：即使所有观察者都改变想法，事实仍会是那样。

senses.title: Seen from outside
senses.titleCN: 从外部看：把自己当成旁观者
senses.definition: by viewing a situation from an external standpoint rather than from inside one's own experience
senses.definitionCN: 从外部立场而非自身经验内部来看待情境
senses.example: She described her own illness objectively, as a case rather than as her life.
senses.exampleCN: 她客观地描述自己的病，把它当成病例而不是自己的人生。
senses.why: The adverb can move the viewpoint: to see oneself objectively is to occupy the position of a stranger looking at the same facts.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以移动视点：客观地看自己，就是站到一个陌生人看同样事实的位置上。

senses.title: Not merely a matter of taste
senses.titleCN: 客观而言：不是“我觉得”，而是“确实”
senses.definition: used to mark a judgement as factual rather than a matter of personal taste
senses.definitionCN: 用来标明某判断属于事实，而非个人口味
senses.example: Objectively, the second route is shorter, whatever the scenery is like.
senses.exampleCN: 客观而言，第二条路线更短，不管风景如何。
senses.why: In conversation the adverb is a signal: it invites the listener to separate the measurable part of a claim from the part that is opinion.
senses.whyCN: 在对话中，这个副词是一种信号：它请听者把主张中可测量的部分与属于意见的部分分开。

senses.title: Even-handedly
senses.titleCN: 不偏不倚：给双方同样的尺子
senses.definition: in a fair manner that applies the same standard to all parties
senses.definitionCN: 对各方适用同一标准的公平方式
senses.example: The chair summed up both proposals objectively before calling the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 主席在表决前不偏不倚地总结了双方提案。
senses.why: Fairness is objectivity applied between people: the same rule is used on both sides, so no one is measured with a shorter ruler.
senses.whyCN: 公平是用于人际之间的客观：同一条规则施于双方，没人被用短尺衡量。

senses.title: By external review
senses.titleCN: 经外部评审：让局外人来核
senses.definition: by means of review conducted by people or methods outside the original group
senses.definitionCN: 由原群体之外的人或方法进行审查的方式
senses.example: The safety record was objectively reviewed by an independent laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 安全记录由一家独立实验室作了客观审查。
senses.why: Institutions secure objectivity by moving the judgement outside: the reviewer has no stake, and the method is published for scrutiny.
senses.whyCN: 机构通过把判断移到外部来确保客观：评审者无利害关系，方法也公开可供审视。

intro.en: Objectively is objective plus -ly. Objective comes from Latin objectum, 'something thrown before', from obicere: ob- 'against' plus iacere 'to throw'.
intro.cn: objectively 是 objective 加 -ly。objective 来自拉丁语 objectum“被抛到面前的东西”，出自 obicere：ob-“对着”加 iacere“投掷”。

items.en: Iacere meant to throw or cast. It is the root of project, reject, inject, and jet, all involving something sent in a direction.
items.cn: iacere 意为投、掷。它是 project、reject、inject、jet 的词根，这些词都含“把某物朝某方向送出”的意思。

items.en: Ob- 'against, before' plus iacere gave obicere, to throw something in front of someone, hence to present or to oppose.
items.cn: ob-“对着、在前”加 iacere 得到 obicere：把东西抛到某人面前，因而表示“呈现”或“反对”。

items.en: Objectum was the thing thrown before the mind or the eyes: an object of thought, of sight, or of an argument.
items.cn: objectum 是被抛到心智或眼睛之前的东西：思想的对象、视觉的对象，或争论的议题。

items.en: Scholastic Latin used objectivus for what exists in the mind as an object of thought, as opposed to what exists in itself.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语用 objectivus 指“作为思想对象存在于心智中的”，与“自身独立存在”的相对。

items.en: English objective reversed the emphasis: it came to mean the thing outside the mind, and hence a judgement free of private feeling.
items.cn: 英语 objective 反转了侧重：它开始指心智之外的事物，因而指不带私人感受的判断。

items.en: Objectively then developed its adverb senses: by evidence, by measurement, from outside, and by independent review.
items.cn: objectively 随后发展出副词义项：依据证据、依据测量、从外部看，以及经独立评审。

note.en: The first group is the object family; the second compares adverbs for judging without personal colour.
note.cn: 第一组是 object 词族；第二组比较几个表示“不带个人色彩地判断”的副词。

entries.definition: a thing that can be seen or touched, or the thing a thought or action is directed at. As a verb it means to oppose.
entries.definitionCN: 可见可触的物体，或思想与行动指向的对象；作动词时表示反对。

entries.definition: based on facts rather than feelings; as a noun, a goal to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 依据事实而非感受的；作名词时指目标。

entries.definition: the quality of judging without personal bias.
entries.definitionCN: 不带个人偏见地判断的品质。

entries.definition: without favouring one party over another. It concerns people and sides, not measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方；关乎人与阵营，而非测量。

entries.definition: without taking either side. It can describe a policy of staying out.
entries.definitionCN: 不站任何一边；可描述置身事外的政策。

entries.definition: with attention to facts. It checks accuracy rather than freedom from bias.
entries.definitionCN: 着眼于事实；检验准确与否，而非是否有偏见。

entries.definition: by reasoning rather than emotion. One can reason rationally from biased premises.
entries.definitionCN: 凭推理而非情绪；但人可以从不偏的前提理性推理，也可以从有偏的前提理性推理。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'before' plus iacere 'throw', then -ive and -ly. The objective is what is thrown in front of everyone to be seen.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“在前”加 iacere“投掷”，再加 -ive 与 -ly。objective 就是被抛到所有人面前、供人看见的东西。

normal.en: Thrown in front: the evidence lies on the table where everyone can see it.
normal.cn: 抛到前面：证据摊在桌上，谁都能看见。

normal.en: A camera in the corner records without having an opinion.
normal.cn: 角落里的摄像机只记录，不发表意见。

normal.en: Objectively measurable means a second lab can get the same number.
normal.cn: 可客观测量，意味着第二个实验室也能得到同一个数。

normal.en: Two reviewers score separately so that the first voice cannot lead the second.
normal.cn: 两位评审分开打分，好让第一个声音带不走第二个。

normal.en: Objective and objection share a root: both put something in front of you.
normal.cn: objective 与 objection 同根：两者都把东西摆到你面前。

abstract.en: Objectivity is not the absence of a viewpoint but the willingness to show where the viewpoint stands.
abstract.cn: 客观不是没有视角，而是愿意把视角的位置摆出来。

abstract.en: Every measuring instrument encodes a decision about what counts, and that decision was made by someone.
abstract.cn: 每件测量仪器都编码了一个“什么才算数”的决定，而这个决定是某个人做的。

abstract.en: To see oneself objectively is to lend one's own life to a stranger for a moment, then take it back.
abstract.cn: 客观地看自己，就是把自己的生活暂借给一个陌生人，然后再收回来。

examples.en: The panel could not judge the design objectively until it agreed on the criteria.
examples.cn: 在就标准达成一致之前，评审组无法客观评判这项设计。

examples.en: Objectively, the old bridge carries less traffic than the new one, whatever residents remember.
examples.cn: 客观而言，旧桥承载的车流少于新桥，不管居民记得什么。

examples.en: The experiment was objectively reviewed by a laboratory that had no funding from the company.
examples.cn: 该实验由一家未接受该公司资助的实验室作了客观审查。

dict_mnemonic.text: object（对象）+ ively——把对象摆到面前看，不掺自己的情绪，就是客观地。

root: 由 objective（客观的）加 -ly 构成；objective 源自拉丁语 objectum“被抛到面前之物”，出自 obicere：ob-“对着、在前”加 iacere“投掷”，故本义为“摆在面前供众人审视”，引申为“不掺私情的判断”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of objectively. They share one move: the judgement is placed outside the judge. It can be outside the judge's feelings, outside the judge's instruments, outside the judge's own experience, or outside the judge's institution.
sensesIntro.cn: objectively 的八个义项共享一个动作：把判断移到判断者之外。它可以移出判断者的情绪、仪器、自身经验，或所属机构之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a camera fixed in the corner of a room, recording every voice and taking no part in the conversation.
core.cn: 核心意象：固定在房间角落的摄像机，录下每个声音，却不参与对话。

chain: LATIN OBJECTUM THE THING SET BEFORE THE MIND
MEDIEVAL OBJECTIVUS EXISTING AS AN OBJECT OF THOUGHT
ENGLISH OBJECTIVE OUTSIDE THE MIND, FACTUAL
OBJECTIVELY WITH THE JUDGEMENT PLACED OUTSIDE THE JUDGE

branches.en: OUTSIDE FEELING AND PRIVATE IMPRESSION: bias set aside, evidence left on the table.
branches.cn: 移出情绪与私人印象：搁下偏见，把证据留在桌上。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE OBSERVER: measurement by instrument and review by an independent body.
branches.cn: 移出观察者：以仪器测量，由独立机构审查。

branches.en: OUTSIDE OPINION: a fact that survives any change of taste, marked in speech as 'not just my view'.
branches.cn: 移出意见：不随口味改变的事实，并在言语中标为“不只是我的看法”。

branches.en: OUTSIDE ONESELF: one's own life described as a case seen from a stranger's chair.
branches.cn: 移出自身：把自己的生活当成从陌生人椅子上看到的病例。

branches.en: OUTSIDE THE PARTY: one standard applied to both sides of an argument.
branches.cn: 移出阵营：用同一把尺子量争论双方。

intro.en: Objectively is objective plus -ly. Objective is object plus -ive, and object goes back to obicere, to throw before. The family also gives objection and objectivity.
intro.cn: objectively 是 objective 加 -ly。objective 是 object 加 -ive，而 object 上溯 obicere“抛到面前”。词族还有 objection 与 objectivity。

latinIntro.en: The base is iacere, to throw, with the prefixed verb obicere and the noun objectum. The same verb underlies project, reject, inject, and subject.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 iacere“投掷”，加前缀的动词 obicere 与名词 objectum。同一动词还构成 project、reject、inject、subject。

items.meaning: a thing perceived or aimed at; as a verb, to oppose
items.meaningCN: 被感知或指向的对象；作动词表示反对
items.example: The object on the table was a sealed box.
items.exampleCN: 桌上的物体是一个封好的盒子。

items.meaning: based on external facts; as a noun, an aim
items.meaningCN: 依据外部事实的；作名词指目标
items.example: The report gives an objective account of the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 报告对争端作了客观叙述。

items.meaningCN: 以无偏见、依据证据的方式
items.example: The two samples were objectively compared.
items.exampleCN: 两个样本被客观地加以比较。

items.meaning: the quality of being free from personal bias
items.meaningCN: 不受个人偏见影响的品质；客观性
items.example: Objectivity requires that the method be public.
items.exampleCN: 客观性要求方法公开。

items.meaning: a statement thrown against a proposal
items.meaningCN: 对提案提出的反对意见
items.example: The lawyer raised an objection to the question.
items.exampleCN: 律师对该问题提出异议。

items.meaning: to cast forward, hence a planned undertaking
items.meaningCN: 向前投出，因而指计划、项目
items.example: The city approved the housing project.
items.exampleCN: 市里批准了这个住房项目。

items.meaning: to throw back, hence to refuse
items.example: The committee rejected the first draft.

items.example: The nurse injected the vaccine into the arm.

intro.en: Donate is a back-formation from donation: the noun came first, from Latin donare, to give as a gift, from donum, a gift, and English later trimmed the noun ending to make a verb.
