definition_zh: 指数；幂；上标数字；阐述者；倡导者；典型代表
definition_en: the power to which a number is raised, or a person who sets out and defends an idea
core_image: 一个数字被抬到另一个数字的右上角，像站在肩膀上
scene: 墙上的公式里，一个数字被抬到字母的右上角，表示连乘的次数。 In the formula, the exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor.
sceneCN: 这里 exponent 指「幂指数，即底数连乘的次数」（第 1 个义项：指数）；句意为公式里的指数说明底数被当作因子用了几次。图中可辨识物件：公式、抬高的数字、粉笔、墙面。

pos.zh: 指数；幂；上标数字；阐述者；倡导者；典型

derivatives.zh: 详述；阐述（同出拉丁 exponere）
使暴露；揭露（同出拉丁 exponere）

senses.title: The power a number is raised to
senses.definition: the number that says how many times a base is multiplied by itself
senses.definitionCN: 说明底数自乘多少次的数
senses.example: In the formula, the exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor.
senses.exampleCN: 在公式里，指数说明底数被当作因子用了几次。
senses.why: exponere means 'to set out'; the exponent sets out how many repetitions the base undergoes.
senses.whyCN: exponere 意为「摆出来」；指数就是把底数重复多少次「摆出来」。

senses.title: The raised figure in notation
senses.definition: the small figure written above and to the right of a base
senses.definitionCN: 写在底数右上方的小数字
senses.example: A raised exponent beside the letter marks repeated multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 字母旁边抬高的指数标出重复相乘。
senses.why: the written position is the visual form of the mathematical idea: the number is literally lifted above the base.
senses.whyCN: 书写位置正是数学想法的可视化：这个数确实被抬到底数上方。

senses.title: A person who explains
senses.definition: someone who sets out and explains a subject in detail
senses.definitionCN: 把某个主题详细摆出来并加以解释的人
senses.example: He became the clearest exponent of the new method in his department.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了本部门里把这种新方法讲得最清楚的人。
senses.why: the Latin participle meant 'setting forth', and a person who sets a subject forth is an expounder.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁分词意为「摆出来」，把主题摆出来的人就是阐述者。

senses.title: A spokesman for a cause
senses.definition: a person who speaks publicly in support of an idea or movement
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某种理念或运动说话的人
senses.example: She was the leading exponent of the reform movement.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这场改革运动的主要代表人物。
senses.why: from explaining a subject it is a short step to speaking for it, so exponent took on the role of public advocate.
senses.whyCN: 从解释一个主题到为它说话只差一步，于是 exponent 承担起公开倡导者的角色。

senses.title: A typical example
senses.definition: a person or thing that shows what a class or style is like
senses.definitionCN: 能显示某一类别或风格是什么样的人或物
senses.example: The little chapel is a fine exponent of the local stone style.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小礼拜堂是当地石构风格的一个很好例证。
senses.why: a thing that sets forth a style is itself the showing of that style, hence 'a typical example'.
senses.whyCN: 把一种风格摆出来的东西，本身就是那种风格的展示，因此引申为「典型例证」。

senses.title: The exponent of a group
senses.definition: the smallest positive power that sends every element of a group to the identity
senses.definitionCN: 使群中每个元素都化为单位元的最小正整数次幂
senses.example: The exponent of the group divides the order of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群的指数整除群的阶。
senses.why: group theory reuses the arithmetic word for the power that makes every element collapse to the identity.
senses.whyCN: 群论把这个算术词挪用来指那个让每个元素都塌回单位元的幂。

senses.title: The exponent of a prime in a factorization
senses.definition: the number showing how many times a prime factor occurs in an integer
senses.definitionCN: 表示某个素因子在一个整数里出现几次的数
senses.example: The exponent of two in twelve is two.
senses.exampleCN: 在十二里，因子二的指数是二。
senses.why: factorization counts repetitions, and the exponent is exactly the written count of those repetitions.
senses.whyCN: 分解数的是重复次数，而指数正是这些重复次数被写下来的结果。

senses.title: A unit that realizes a linguistic feature
senses.definition: a sound or form that carries a particular grammatical feature
senses.definitionCN: 承载某一语法特征的具体语音或形式
senses.example: The past-tense ending is the exponent of tense in that verb.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个动词里，过去时词尾是时态的体现形式。
senses.why: linguistics borrows the 'setting forth' idea: a form sets forth an abstract feature in audible shape.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了「摆出来」的想法：某个形式把抽象特征以可听见的形态摆出来。

senses.title: The exponent in scientific notation
senses.definition: the power of ten that scales a number in scientific notation
senses.definitionCN: 科学记数法中用来缩放数值的十的幂
senses.example: Changing the exponent moved the decimal point six places.
senses.exampleCN: 改变指数把小数点移动了六位。
senses.why: in scientific notation the exponent is the part that records how far the decimal point has been shifted.
senses.whyCN: 在科学记数法里，指数就是记录小数点被移动了多远的那个部分。

intro.en: Exponent comes from Latin exponens, the present participle of exponere 'to put out, set forth, explain', built on ex- 'out' and ponere 'to put, place'. The mathematical sense was added in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: exponent 来自拉丁 exponens，即 exponere「摆出来、陈述、解释」的现在分词，由 ex-「出」与 ponere「放、置」构成。数学义是十七世纪才加上的。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. It is one of the most productive Latin verbs in English compounds: component, postpone, compose and deposit all descend from it.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。它是英语复合词中最能产的拉丁动词之一：component、postpone、compose 与 deposit 都出自它。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere gave exponere 'to put out, set forth, expose, explain'. The same verb produced both expose and expound in English.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere 构成 exponere「摆出来、陈述、暴露、解释」。同一个动词在英语里既产生 expose，也产生 expound。

items.en: The present participle exponens named one who sets something forth, hence an expounder or interpreter.
items.cn: 现在分词 exponens 指把某事物摆出来的人，因此是阐述者、解释者。

items.en: English took exponent first as a noun for a person who explains or interprets a text or doctrine.
items.cn: 英语最初把 exponent 用作名词，指解释或诠释文本、教义的人。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the word was applied to the raised number that shows a power, since it 'sets forth' how many times the base is repeated.
items.cn: 十七世纪时，这个词被用来指右上角表示幂的数，因为它把底数重复了多少次「摆出来」。

items.en: The exact first mathematical citation is approximate; the Latin verb itself and its participle are securely attested.
items.cn: 数学义的最早确切书证年代为约数；但这个拉丁动词及其分词本身有可靠记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb ponere 'to put' and is a constant source of confusion; the second group names people or numbers with a comparable role.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 ponere「放」，是持续不断的混淆来源；第二组是角色相近的人或数。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: a part put together with others into a whole; it is not an exponent.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「共同」的前缀加 ponere：与其他部分拼成整体的一个部件；并非指数。

entries.definition: Post- 'after' plus ponere: to put something off to a later time.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「之后」的前缀加 ponere：把事情放到更晚的时间。

entries.definition: Also from exponere, but through French: to put something out where it can be seen, hence to uncover.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 exponere，但经法语而来：把东西摆到能被看见的地方，因此指揭露、暴露。

entries.definition: From exponere through Old French: to set out an idea at length; it is the verb behind the 'explainer' sense of exponent.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 exponere，经古法语而来：详细陈述一个想法；它正是 exponent「阐述者」义背后的动词。

entries.definition: Ob- 'against' plus ponere: one who sets himself against another, not one who sets a subject forth.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「对着」的前缀加 ponere：把自己摆到别人对面的人，而非把主题摆出来的人。

entries.definition: In arithmetic, the result of repeated multiplication or the number of repetitions; it overlaps with exponent but can also mean the result.
entries.definitionCN: 在算术里指重复相乘的结果或次数；与指数重叠，但也常指结果本身。

entries.tag: another name for the raised number
entries.definition: A synonym for exponent in older mathematical writing; it also means a pointer or a list.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的数学文献里是 exponent 的同义词；它另指指针或索引。

entries.definition: A person who argues publicly for a cause; it matches the 'spokesman' sense without the explanatory tone.
entries.definitionCN: 公开为某项事业辩护的人；对应「代言人」义，但不带解释的色彩。

entries.definition: One who puts a proposal forward; it is built on the same putting verb, ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 提出并支持某项主张的人；同样由那个表示「放」的动词构成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus ponere 'put': the exponent is the number put out above the base.
normal.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere「放」：指数就是被放到底数上方的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs exponent, exponential, exponentially, exponentiation and expound.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exponent、exponential、exponentially、exponentiation 与 expound。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the two lives of the word: fractional exponent, and chief exponent of a movement.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这个词的两条命：分数指数，以及某项运动的主要倡导者。

normal.en: The same ponere builds component, postpone and opponent, all about placing something somewhere.
normal.cn: 同一个 ponere 还构成 component、postpone 与 opponent，都是把某物放到某处。

normal.en: In a power, the base carries the weight and the exponent rides on its shoulder.
normal.cn: 在幂里，底数扛着重量，指数骑在它肩上。

abstract.en: Picture a small figure standing on a tall number's shoulder, counting how many times it is copied.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小人站在一个大数的肩膀上，数它被复制了多少次。

abstract.en: Picture a lecturer lifting a heavy idea above the crowd so everyone can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位讲演者把一个沉重的想法举过人群头顶，让所有人都看见。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a bottle that tells you how concentrated the contents are.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶子上贴着标签，告诉你里面的东西浓缩到什么程度。

examples.en: A negative exponent turns the base into a fraction.
examples.cn: 负指数会把底数变成一个分数。

examples.en: She became the public exponent of a quieter style of architecture.
examples.cn: 她成了那种更安静的建筑风格的公开倡导者。

examples.en: The exponent on the ten shows how far the decimal point has moved.
examples.cn: 十上面的指数显示小数点移动了多远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯破能」——把「能」一层层破开叠到右上角 → 指数

root: 拉丁 exponere「摆出来、陈述」= ex-（出）+ ponere（放、置）→ exponens「摆出来的人／摆出来的东西」。英语 exponent，数学义十七世纪起。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split between two gestures: a number lifted above a base, and a person who lifts an idea into public view. Both come from the same Latin verb for setting something out.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分成两个动作：一个数被抬到底数上方，一个人把一个想法抬到公众眼前。两者都出自同一个表示「摆出来」的拉丁动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one number standing on the shoulder of another, counting repetitions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个数站在另一个数的肩膀上，数重复的次数。

branches.en: RAISED POWER: the count of repetitions and the small figure written above the base.
branches.cn: 抬高的幂：重复的次数，以及写在底数上方的小数字。

branches.en: PERSON WHO EXPLAINS: one who sets a subject out in detail.
branches.cn: 解释的人：把主题详细摆出来的人。

branches.en: SPEAKING SAMPLE: the advocate speaks for a movement, and the little chapel speaks for a style.
branches.cn: 会说话的样本：倡导者为运动说话，小礼拜堂为一种风格说话。

branches.en: COUNTING POWER: group theory and prime factorization both use the raised number as a tally.
branches.cn: 计数的幂：群论与素因子分解都把那个抬高的数当作计数。

branches.en: REALIZED FORM: a suffix carries an abstract feature, and a power of ten carries a shifted decimal point.
branches.cn: 体现出来的形式：词尾承载抽象特征，十的幂承载被移动的小数点。

intro.en: Exponent is a Latin participle of a verb built from a prefix and the common verb for placing; the same pieces build many English words.
intro.cn: exponent 是一个拉丁分词，其动词由前缀与那个最常用的「放」动词构成；这些构件还构成许多英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere gives component, postpone, compose, deposit and opponent; ex- adds the sense of putting something out into view.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere 衍生 component、postpone、compose、deposit 与 opponent；ex- 增添「把东西摆到可见处」的意思。

items.example: The prefix pulls the idea out where it can be seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把想法拉到能被看见的地方。

items.example: The root is the plain act of placing something.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是放置东西的朴素动作。

items.meaning: to put out, set forth, explain
items.example: The verb covers both exposing and explaining.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既包括暴露，也包括解释。

items.meaning: setting forth; one who sets forth
items.example: The participle became both adjective and noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词既作形容词，也作名词。

items.example: The exponent sits above the base.
items.exampleCN: 指数坐在底数上方。

items.example: The curve is exponential in shape.
items.exampleCN: 这条曲线在形状上是指数的。

items.meaning: the operation of raising to a power
items.example: Exponentiation grows faster than multiplication.
items.exampleCN: 求幂比乘法增长得快。

items.meaning: a part placed together with others
items.meaningCN: 与其他部分拼在一起的部件
items.example: Each component was tested alone.
items.exampleCN: 每个部件都单独测试过。

items.example: They postponed the launch by a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们把发射推迟了一周。

latinEntries.meaning: to put out, set forth, explain
setting forth; one who sets forth

derivatives.zh: 详述；阐述（同出拉丁 exponere）
使暴露；揭露（同出拉丁 exponere）

definition_zh: 受制于；须遵守；易遭受；须经（批准或条件），表示处于某种约束或可能之下
definition_en: to be governed by a rule, exposed to a risk, or conditional upon something else
core_image: 一块木牌挂在铁链下，牌上压着一枚公章，链子的另一端钉在墙上
scene: 墙边一块木牌被铁链拴住，牌上盖着公章，链头钉在墙上。 All such exports will be subject to a licence.
sceneCN: 这里指这类出口须经许可（第 3 个义项：须经批准）；句意为所有这类出口都将受许可证约束。图中可辨识物件：木牌、铁链、公章、墙面。

pos.zh: 形容词短语：受制于；易遭受
固定搭配：以……为条件

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「置于其下」的分词而来，义为「主题；受制于」
由该分词加名词尾构成，义为「征服；服从」
由该词干加形容词尾构成，义为「主观的」
由该名词加「内容」构成的复合词，义为「题材」
由该分词加被动结构构成，义为「被施加；遭受」

senses.title: Bound by a rule
senses.definition: to be required to obey a law or regulation
senses.definitionCN: 必须遵守法律或规章
senses.example: All such exports will be subject to a licence.
senses.exampleCN: 所有这类出口都将受许可证约束。
senses.why: The image is of something placed under an authority, so the rule sits above the thing and governs it.
senses.whyCN: 意象是把某物置于权威之下，规则因此高悬其上并管着它。

senses.title: Exposed to harm
senses.definition: to be open to damage, disease or loss
senses.definitionCN: 暴露在损害、疾病或损失之下
senses.example: These crops can be subject to frost damage.
senses.exampleCN: 这些作物可能遭受霜冻损害。
senses.why: Here the thing hangs under a risk rather than under a rule, but the grammar is the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里悬在风险而非规则之下，但语法结构相同。

senses.title: Requiring approval
senses.definition: to need permission or a formal step before it can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 必须先取得许可或完成正式程序
senses.example: Any change to the design must be subject to review.
senses.exampleCN: 设计的任何改动都必须经过评审。
senses.why: Approval is a gate placed above the thing, so nothing moves until it opens.
senses.whyCN: 批准是设在上方的一道门，门不开就动不了。

senses.title: Conditional on something
senses.definition: to depend on a condition that may alter it
senses.definitionCN: 取决于某项可能改变它的条件
senses.example: Prices may be subject to change without notice.
senses.exampleCN: 价格可能变动，恕不另行通知。
senses.why: A condition is written into the frame, so the statement is true only while the condition holds.
senses.whyCN: 条件被写进框架，因此陈述只在条件成立时有效。

senses.title: Affected by a force
senses.definition: to be liable to be affected by fluctuations or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 易受波动或压力的影响
senses.example: The results can be subject to seasonal swings.
senses.exampleCN: 结果可能受季节波动影响。
senses.why: An external force pushes the thing, and the frame records that it cannot resist.
senses.whyCN: 外力推动某物，框架记录的是它无法抗拒。

senses.title: Under a jurisdiction
senses.definition: to fall under the legal or political authority of a body
senses.definitionCN: 处于某机构的法律或政治管辖之下
senses.example: The islands will be subject to local law.
senses.exampleCN: 这些岛屿将受当地法律管辖。
senses.why: Jurisdiction is authority over a place, the same image of standing under applied to territory.
senses.whyCN: 管辖是对一片地方的权威，仍是「处于其下」的意象用于领土。

senses.title: Awaiting confirmation
senses.definition: used when a figure or plan is not yet final
senses.definitionCN: 数字或计划尚未最终确定时使用
senses.example: The dates may be subject to confirmation.
senses.exampleCN: 日期可能还有待确认。
senses.why: This sense is a polite hedge: the thing is true for now but can still move.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是礼貌的留白：目前成立，但仍可能变动。

senses.title: Under someone's power
senses.definition: to be controlled by a person or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 处于某人或某权威的控制之下
senses.example: No official can be subject to pressure from a single firm.
senses.exampleCN: 任何官员都不应受单一公司的压力支配。
senses.why: Power is the personal form of the same relation: one party stands above another.
senses.whyCN: 权力是同一关系的个人形式：一方高居另一方之上。

intro.en: Subject comes from Latin subiectus, the past participle of subicere, to throw under, from sub-, under, and iacere, to throw. The adjective use with to is a later English development; its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: subject 源自拉丁语 subiectus，是 subicere 的过去分词，后者由 sub-「在下」与 iacere「投掷」构成，意为「置于其下」。与介词连用的形容词用法是较晚的英语发展，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Iacere means to throw and also underlies project, reject and inject.
items.cn: iacere 意为「投掷」，也是 project、reject、inject 的根基。

items.en: Sub- means under, so the compound pictures something thrown beneath.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下」，复合词画出某物被投到下面。

items.en: Subicere means to place under, to submit or to subject.
items.cn: subicere 意为「置于其下、使服从」。

items.en: The participle names the thing placed under an authority.
items.cn: 分词指被置于权威之下的东西。

items.en: English uses subject as noun and adjective; the frame with to marks what governs it.
items.cn: 英语中该词作名词与形容词；带介词的框架标出支配者。

items.en: The fixed frame is modern; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 固定框架属近代用法，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group looks nearly identical but reverses the direction of the action; the second group holds other ways of stating exposure or condition.
note.cn: 第一组形近但动作方向相反；第二组是其他表述「暴露」或「条件」的说法。

entries.definition: It means someone actively imposes something on the subject; this phrase describes a standing condition.
entries.definitionCN: 它指有人主动把某事施加于对象；本短语只描述持续状态。

entries.definition: The shorter form works as a modifier, as in prices subject to change.
entries.definitionCN: 较短形式作修饰语，如「可能变动的价格」。

entries.definition: Alone it means a topic, a person under rule, or a grammatical subject.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时指主题、受治者或语法主语。

entries.definition: It describes what belongs to a person's view, from the same root but a different branch.
entries.definitionCN: 它描述属于个人看法的东西，同根但另一分支。

entries.definition: It stresses legal or physical exposure, close to the risk sense.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调法律或身体上的暴露，接近「风险」义。

entries.definition: It stresses an inner tendency to suffer something.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调内在的易发倾向。

entries.definition: It names the rule or promise that constrains, without the risk sense.
entries.definitionCN: 它点出约束的规则或承诺，不带风险义。

entries.definition: It states that one thing follows from another, close to the conditional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 它说明一物取决于另一物，接近「条件」义。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Latin throw, the active-passive contrast and the three core layers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语「投掷」、主动与被动的对比以及三层核心义。

normal.en: Iacere is to throw, so subject means thrown under something.
normal.cn: 词根意为「投掷」，subject 就是被投到某物之下。

normal.en: The three core layers are rule, risk and approval.
normal.cn: 三层核心义是规则、风险与批准。

normal.en: Be subjected to is an action; be subject to is a state.
normal.cn: 一个是被施加的动作，一个是持续的状态。

normal.en: With change and confirmation, the phrase becomes a polite hedge.
normal.cn: 与「变动」「确认」连用时，短语变成礼貌留白。

normal.en: The same root gives subjective, which is about opinion, not rule.
normal.cn: 同根词「主观的」关乎看法，与规则无关。

abstract.en: Like a wooden board chained to a wall with a seal stamped on it.
abstract.cn: 像木牌被铁链拴在墙上，牌上盖着公章。

abstract.en: Like a boat tied to a dock: it floats, but it cannot drift away.
abstract.cn: 像系在码头的船：能浮，却漂不走。

abstract.en: Like a price tag with a small note saying it may change.
abstract.cn: 像价签上附一行小字，写着可能变动。

examples.en: All such exports will be subject to a licence.
examples.cn: 所有这类出口都将受许可证约束。

examples.en: These crops can be subject to frost damage.
examples.cn: 这些作物可能遭受霜冻损害。

examples.en: The dates may be subject to confirmation.
examples.cn: 日期可能还有待确认。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「比 萨布杰克特 图」——木牌被铁链拴在墙上，牌上盖着公章：受制于；须经

root: subject 源自拉丁语 subiectus，是 subicere 的过去分词，后者由表示「在下」的前缀与 iacere「投掷」构成；形容词与介词连用的框架是较晚的英语发展，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by what governs the subject: a rule, a harm, an approval step, a condition, a force, a jurisdiction, a pending confirmation and a person's power.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按支配者区分：规则、伤害、审批环节、条件、外力、司法管辖、待确认、他人权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden board chained to a wall with an official seal stamped on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：木牌被铁链拴在墙上，牌上盖着公章。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: a law or a jurisdiction sits above the subject and governs it.
branches.cn: 权威：法律或辖区高居其上并治理它。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL POWER: one party stands above another, the same relation in human form.
branches.cn: 人身权力：一方高居另一方之上，是同一关系的人身形式。

branches.en: THE EXPOSURE: harm and fluctuation hang over the thing that cannot resist.
branches.cn: 暴露：伤害与波动悬在无力抗拒之物上。

branches.en: THE GATE: approval must be passed before anything proceeds.
branches.cn: 关口：未过审批就不能推进。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: change and confirmation keep the statement provisional.
branches.cn: 条件：变动与确认让陈述保持临时性。

intro.en: The Latin core is sub-, under, plus iacere, to throw; subicere and its participle subiectus give the English word.
intro.cn: 拉丁核心是 sub-「在下」加 iacere「投掷」；subicere 及其分词提供英语词形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin elements are sub-, under, and iacere, to throw; subicere joins them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 sub-「在下」与 iacere「投掷」，subicere 由两者合成。

items.example: The prefix puts the thing beneath something else.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把某物置于另一物之下。

items.example: The verb also gives project and reject.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也给出「投射」「拒绝」诸词。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 复合动词是英语词形的直接来源。

items.example: The participle becomes the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 分词成为英语形容词。

items.example: The word serves as noun, adjective and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼作名词、形容词与动词。

items.meaning: the state of being under control
items.example: The noun names the state of being placed under.
items.exampleCN: 名词指被置于其下的状态。

items.example: The branch shifts from rule to opinion.
items.exampleCN: 这一分支从规则转向看法。

items.example: The frame fixes the governing thing after the preposition.
items.exampleCN: 框架把支配者固定在介词后。

latinEntries.structure: iacere, iacio, ieci, iactum (verb, third conjugation)

definition_zh: 反方论点；针对某一主张提出的反对论证；文章或辩论中先摆出的对立观点
definition_en: an argument that opposes or challenges another argument, often presented before it is answered
core_image: 两个人对坐，桌上一张纸写着主张，另一张纸从对面推过来，写着相反的推论
scene: 论文写到第三段，作者先把可能反对自己的一方意见完整摆出来，再准备逐条回应。 The essay admits a strong counterargument before defending its thesis.
sceneCN: 这里指先摆出来的对立观点（第 1 个义项：反对某一主张的论证）；句意为这篇文章在为自己的论点辩护之前，先承认一个强有力的反方论点。

pos.zh: 反方论点；反对论证

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「使清楚、证明」而来的名词，义为「论证；论点」
同源动词，义为「论证；争辩」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「好争辩的；论证性的」
由拉丁语「反对」而来的前缀，义为「反；对应」
由同一前缀加「主张」构成，义为「反诉；相反主张」

senses.title: An argument that opposes a thesis
senses.definition: a set of reasons put forward to show that another argument or claim is wrong or weak
senses.definitionCN: 为表明另一论证或主张有误或站不住而提出的一组理由
senses.example: The strongest counterargument is that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 最强的反方论点是样本太小。
senses.why: Counter- adds opposition to argument, so the word names the other side of a contested claim.
senses.whyCN: 前缀给「论证」加上对立，因此这个词指有争议主张的另一面。

senses.title: The opposing case in a debate
senses.definition: the body of argument that the opposing team or speaker presents
senses.definitionCN: 对方队伍或发言人提出的整套论证
senses.example: The negative team built its counterargument around cost.
senses.exampleCN: 反方队伍围绕成本构建了它的对立论证。
senses.why: Debate is organised into sides, and each side's case is literally an argument set against the other.
senses.whyCN: 辩论分成正反两方，每一方的立论就是对着另一方摆出的论证。

senses.title: The fairness paragraph of an essay
senses.titleCN: 文章中体现公允的段落
senses.definition: the part of an essay that states the opposing view before answering it
senses.definitionCN: 文章在回应之前先陈述对立观点的部分
senses.example: A short counterargument paragraph makes the paper look fair.
senses.exampleCN: 一段简短的反方论点使文章显得公允。
senses.why: Academic writing treats the opposing view as a required move, so the word also names that paragraph.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把对立观点当作必要的一步，因此这个词也指那一段。

senses.title: A rival explanation in research
senses.definition: an alternative explanation that could account for the same observations
senses.definitionCN: 能对同一批观察给出解释的另一种说法
senses.example: The authors tested a counterargument based on weather rather than policy.
senses.exampleCN: 作者检验了一个基于天气而非政策提出的竞争性解释。
senses.why: In science the opponent is not a person but another explanation, and it must be ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 在科学里，对手不是人而是另一种解释，它必须被排除。

senses.title: A hypothetical objection used as a test
senses.titleCN: 用作检验的假想反对意见
senses.definition: an objection thought up to stress-test a claim before it is published
senses.definitionCN: 在发表之前用来压力测试某一主张而想出的反对意见
senses.example: She wrote the strongest counterargument she could imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 她写下了自己能想到的最强反方论点。
senses.why: Imagining the opposition is a method, since a claim that survives a hard objection is stronger.
senses.whyCN: 想象反对意见是一种方法，经得住严厉质疑的主张更稳固。

senses.title: The opposing legal case
senses.definition: the version of facts and law that the opposing party argues in a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 争议中对方当事人所主张的事实与法律版本
senses.example: Counsel spent the morning preparing a counterargument on jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 律师整个上午都在准备关于管辖权的反方论证。
senses.why: Litigation is an argument with consequences, and each party's case is a counterargument to the other's.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼是带后果的论证，每一方的主张都是对另一方主张的反论。

senses.title: A challenge to a policy
senses.definition: a reasoned objection to a proposed measure or official plan
senses.definitionCN: 对拟议措施或官方计划提出的有理有据的反对
senses.example: The committee heard a counterargument from the small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会听取了小企业提出的反方论证。
senses.why: Policy debate reproduces the academic form, with objections stated before decisions are taken.
senses.whyCN: 政策辩论复制了学术的形式：在作出决定前先陈述反对意见。

senses.title: A move that shows balance
senses.definition: the rhetorical act of presenting the other view so that one's own case appears measured
senses.definitionCN: 先呈现对方观点、使自己的立场显得持中的修辞动作
senses.example: The speaker opened with a counterargument to win the audience's trust.
senses.exampleCN: 发言者先抛出一个反方论点来赢得听众信任。
senses.why: Stating the other side first is a way of borrowing its credibility, which is why the move is taught explicitly.
senses.whyCN: 先讲对方一面是借取其公信力的办法，所以这一招被明确写进写作教材。

intro.en: Counterargument is a transparent compound: a Latin prefix meaning against joined to a Latin word for a reasoned argument. The word names the opposing case itself, not the answer to it.
intro.cn: 这是一个构词透明的组合：表示「反对」的拉丁前缀，加上表示「有理据的论证」的拉丁词。它指对立方的主张本身，而不是对它的回应。

items.en: Contra meant against or opposite, and it survives in English prefixes and in words such as contradict.
items.cn: 这个词意为「反对、相对」，至今保存在英语前缀以及「反驳」一类词里。

items.en: Arguere meant to make clear, to prove, and also to accuse; the proving sense fed the modern word for argument.
items.cn: 这个词意为「使清楚、证明」，也指指控；其中「证明」义喂养了现代的「论证」一词。

items.en: Argumentum named the content of a proof, and English took argument through French with the same core.
items.cn: 这个词指证明的内容，英语经法语引入「论证」，核心义相同。

items.en: Old French used contre- for opposition in compounds, and English borrowed the pattern.
items.cn: 古法语用这一前缀表示复合词中的对立，英语借用了这种构词方式。

items.en: The compound appeared in English in the nineteenth century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十九世纪的英语中出现；确切的最早记录不确定。

items.en: Composition teaching fixed counterargument as the paragraph that states the other view, making it a classroom term.
items.cn: 写作教学把「反方论点」固定为陈述对方观点的那一段，使它成为课堂术语。

note.en: The first group shares the argument root or the opposition prefix; the second group names the answer rather than the opposing case.
note.cn: 第一组共享「论证」词根或「反对」前缀；第二组指回应，而不是对立方的主张。

entries.definition: A set of reasons offered in support of a position.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一立场提供的一组理由。

entries.definition: To give reasons for or against something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为或反对某事给出理由。

entries.definition: A claim set against another claim, often in law.
entries.definitionCN: 指对着另一主张提出的主张，常用于法律。

entries.definition: A contrasting element; its root is a point, not an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成对照的要素；词根是「点」，不是「论证」。

entries.definition: A case that disproves a general statement.
entries.definitionCN: 指推翻一般性陈述的反例。

entries.definition: To meet unexpectedly; it looks like counter but comes from a meeting prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指意外相遇；形似却来自表示相遇的前缀。

entries.definition: The answer that tries to disprove the opposing argument, not the opposing argument itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指试图驳倒对方论证的回应，而不是对方论证本身。

entries.definition: A stated reason for opposing something, often shorter than a full argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对某事的理由，通常比完整论证短。

entries.definition: The act of proving an argument false.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某论证为假的行为。

entries.definition: The position held by those who disagree, stated without the full reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同意者的立场，未必带完整推理。

entries.definition: A call to justify a claim, weaker than a worked-out argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求为某主张给出理由，比完整论证弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two papers facing each other, the essay paragraph and the debate side.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两张对推的纸、作文里的那一段与辩论中的一方。

normal.en: Counter means against and argument means reasons, so the word is simply the reasons against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「反对」，后一半意为「理由」，所以这个词就是「反对的理由」。

normal.en: The essay phrase is «acknowledge the counterargument», a standard move in composition.
normal.cn: 作文里的固定说法是「承认反方论点」，是写作中的标准动作。

normal.en: A counterargument is not a rebuttal: one is the punch, the other is the block.
normal.cn: 反方论点不是反驳：一个是打出的拳，一个是挡回的格。

normal.en: A counterexample is a single case; a counterargument is a whole case against you.
normal.cn: 反例是一个事例，反方论点则是整套反对你的理由。

normal.en: In debate the negative team's whole case can be called the counterargument.
normal.cn: 在辩论中，反方队伍的整体立论可称为反方论点。

abstract.en: A counterargument is the shadow that proves the light exists, since a claim with no opposition is not yet a claim.
abstract.cn: 反方论点是证明光存在的影子，因为无人反对的主张还称不上主张。

abstract.en: Arguing against yourself is the cheapest way to find out what you actually believe.
abstract.cn: 与自己争辩，是弄清自己真正相信什么的最省力的办法。

abstract.en: Every strong case carries its opponent inside it from the beginning.
abstract.cn: 每个强立论从一开始就把对手装在自己体内。

examples.en: The paper addresses the main counterargument in a single paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇论文用一段回应了主要的反方论点。

examples.en: Ignoring a counterargument makes a proposal look weak.
examples.cn: 忽视反方论点会让提案显得薄弱。

examples.en: She offered a counterargument based on the cost of the scheme.
examples.cn: 她基于该方案的成本提出了一个反方论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「反」加「论证」：对着你的主张推回来的那套理由，就是反方论点

root: 前缀来自拉丁语 contra「反对、相对」；后一半来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明的内容」，其动词 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明」。古法语用对立前缀构词，英语借用；复合词在十九世纪出现，写作教学在二十世纪把它固定为「陈述对方观点的那一段」。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the claim to the classroom: an opposing argument, a debate side, the fairness paragraph, a rival explanation, a hypothetical test, the legal case, a policy challenge, and a balancing move.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从主张延伸到课堂：反对论证、辩论一方、公允段落、竞争性解释、假想检验、法律主张、政策质疑、平衡姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sheets of paper travel toward each other across a table, each carrying reasons against the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张纸在桌面上相互推近，各自写着反对对方的理由。

branches.en: THE OPPOSING CASE: reasons set against a claim, whether in writing or in debate.
branches.cn: 对立的主张：对着某一论点摆出的理由，无论书面还是辩论。

branches.en: THE FAIRNESS MOVE: stating the other view first so one's own case looks measured.
branches.cn: 公允之举：先讲对方观点，使自己的立场显得持中。

branches.en: THE RIVAL EXPLANATION: another account of the same facts, waiting to be ruled out.
branches.cn: 竞争性解释：对同一批事实的另一说法，等着被排除。

branches.en: THE SELF-TEST: an objection invented to try to break one's own claim.
branches.cn: 自我检验：为击破自身主张而想出的反对意见。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE ARENA: the legal case and the policy objection.
branches.cn: 外部场域：法律上的对方主张与政策质疑。

intro.en: Counterargument is a compound of a Latin opposition prefix and a Latin argument word, and neither half has changed meaning.
intro.cn: 这个词组由拉丁语的对立前缀与论证词构成，两半的含义都没有改变。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies contra and argumentum; English supplies the combining habit that made them one word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「反对」与「论证」，英语提供了把它们合成一个词的构词习惯。

items.example: It marks the opposing side of a claim.
items.exampleCN: 它标出主张的对立一面。

items.example: The root of the argument family.
items.exampleCN: 这是「论证」一族的词根。

items.example: It became English argument.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「论证」。

items.example: It forms the compound with argument.
items.exampleCN: 它与「论证」合成这个复合词。

items.meaning: the result or means of an action
items.example: It marks the noun argument.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「论证」。

items.example: The same pattern applied to law.
items.exampleCN: 同一构词方式用于法律。

items.meaning: a case against a general claim
items.example: The same prefix applied to a case.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀用于「事例」。

items.example: It is the response, not the opposing case.
items.exampleCN: 它是回应，而非对方主张。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁「证明的内容」经法语而来，义为「论证；论点」
同源动词，义为「论证；争辩」
加形容词尾，义为「好争辩的」
同前缀复合，义为「反诉；相反主张」

definition_zh: 适应的；有适应能力的；可自我调节的
definition_en: able to change in order to fit new conditions, or relating to the process of such change
core_image: 一把能随地形改变齿距的钥匙，插进去总能咬住锁芯
scene: 越野车驶过沙地、碎石与泥坑。 The suspension softens on sand and hardens on gravel, and the car crosses all three surfaces without changing a single part, because the system is adaptive.
sceneCN: 这里 adaptive 是「能随环境自我调节的」（第 1 个义项：能适应新条件）；句意：悬挂在沙地上变软、在碎石上变硬，这辆车不换一个零件就通过三种地形，因为这套系统能自适应。图中可辨识物件：越野车、沙地、碎石、泥坑、变化中的悬挂。

pos.zh: 适应的；有适应能力的
自适应调节的
（生物）适应性的

collocations.zh: 适应性再利用（旧建筑改用途）

senses.title: Able to adjust to new conditions
senses.definition: capable of changing behaviour or structure in order to fit a new situation
senses.definitionCN: 能够改变行为或结构以适应新情境
senses.example: Small teams are more adaptive than large bureaucracies.
senses.exampleCN: 小团队比大型官僚机构更具适应性。
senses.why: Adaptive is adapt plus -ive, 'tending to'. The suffix names a disposition rather than a completed act: something adaptive is built to keep fitting, not fitted once.
senses.whyCN: adaptive 是 adapt 加 -ive“倾向于”。这个后缀命名一种倾向，而不是一次完成的动作：adaptive 的东西被造出来是为了持续适合，而不是适合一次。

senses.title: A trait that raises fitness
senses.definition: in biology, of a trait, increasing an organism's chance of survival and reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指性状提高生物生存与繁殖的机会
senses.example: Camouflage is adaptive in open grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 在开阔草原上，伪装具有适应性。
senses.why: Evolution uses the adjective for whatever the environment rewards. 'Adaptive' does not mean 'changed' but 'changed in a way that pays', so the word carries an implicit judgement about fitness.
senses.whyCN: 演化用这个形容词指环境所奖励的任何东西。adaptive 不是“改变过的”，而是“改变得有利的”，因此这个词隐含了对适应度的判断。

senses.title: An immune system that learns
senses.definition: of immunity, acquired after exposure and able to recognize a specific pathogen
senses.definitionCN: 指暴露后获得、能识别特定病原体的免疫
senses.example: Adaptive immunity remembers the virus and responds faster next time.
senses.exampleCN: 适应性免疫记住这种病毒，下次反应更快。
senses.why: The immune system literally adapts: it edits its repertoire after meeting an antigen. The word's 'fit to' core becomes a memory that is written into cells.
senses.whyCN: 免疫系统确实在适应：遇到抗原后它会编辑自己的库。这个词“使适合”的核心变成写入细胞里的记忆。

senses.title: A system that responds to input
senses.titleCN: 能对输入作出反应的系统
senses.definition: of software or machinery, changing its behaviour according to signals from its environment
senses.definitionCN: 指软件或机械根据环境信号改变行为
senses.example: The adaptive controller adjusts the dose as the sensor readings change.
senses.exampleCN: 自适应控制器随传感器读数变化调整剂量。
senses.why: Engineering makes the adjective technical: a system measures its own performance and corrects it. The fit is now a feedback loop, repeated many times a second.
senses.whyCN: 工程使这个形容词技术化：系统测量自身表现并作出修正。此时的“适合”是一个反馈回路，每秒重复多次。

senses.title: Behaviour that meets a new situation
senses.definition: of behaviour, flexible and appropriate to an unfamiliar or changing situation
senses.definitionCN: 指行为灵活，适合陌生或变化中的情境
senses.example: Adaptive behaviour includes asking for help when a plan fails.
senses.exampleCN: 适应行为包括在计划失败时寻求帮助。
senses.why: Here the flexible thing is not a body or a machine but a response. The word describes a repertoire that can be recombined, which is why it appears in psychology and education.
senses.whyCN: 这里灵活的不是身体或机器，而是反应。这个词描述一套可以被重新组合的行为库，因此常见于心理学与教育学。

senses.title: Adaptive reuse of a building
senses.titleCN: 旧建筑的适应性再利用
senses.definition: in architecture, the conversion of an old structure for a new use while keeping its fabric
senses.definitionCN: 建筑中指保留旧结构主体、改用新用途
senses.example: The warehouse's adaptive reuse turned it into a library.
senses.exampleCN: 这座仓库的适应性再利用把它变成了图书馆。
senses.why: A building cannot be redesigned from scratch without cost, so it is refitted. Adaptive reuse is the tailoring image at architectural scale: keep the coat, change its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 建筑无法不计成本地推倒重来，因此被改装。适应性再利用是建筑尺度上的裁缝画面：保留外套，改变用途。

senses.title: Adaptive management
senses.definition: in policy and ecology, a way of managing that treats decisions as experiments and adjusts them as evidence arrives
senses.definitionCN: 政策与生态学中把决策当作实验、随证据调整的管理方式
senses.example: Adaptive management let the park change its burn plan after the first results.
senses.exampleCN: 适应性管理让公园在首批结果出来后修改了烧除计划。
senses.why: The word turns management into a loop rather than a plan. Each action produces information, and the next action is fitted to that information, so adaptation becomes institutional.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把管理变成回路，而不是计划。每个行动产生信息，下一个行动再适合这些信息，于是适应成为制度性的。

senses.title: Adaptive radiation in evolution
senses.definition: in evolution, the rapid diversification of one lineage into many forms that fill different niches
senses.definitionCN: 演化中指一个谱系迅速分化为许多形态，占据不同生态位
senses.example: The finches are a classic case of adaptive radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些雀鸟是适应辐射的经典案例。
senses.why: Radiation is adaptation multiplied: one body plan is refitted to many diets and habitats. The word describes divergence driven by fitting, not by a single clever change.
senses.whyCN: 辐射是适应乘以许多次：一套身体方案被改到许多食性与栖息地。这个词描述由“适合”驱动的分化，而不是由一次聪明的改变驱动。

intro.en: Adaptive is a derived adjective: adapt plus -ive. The suffix marks a tendency or capacity, so adaptive describes something built to keep fitting rather than something already fitted.
intro.cn: adaptive 是派生形容词：adapt 加 -ive。这个后缀标记倾向或能力，因此 adaptive 描述“被造来持续适合”的东西，而不是“已经适合”的东西。

items.en: Adaptare 'fit to' is ad- 'to' plus aptare 'fit', from aptus 'suited'. The base image is one thing made to match another.
items.cn: adaptare“使适合”是 ad-“向”加 aptare“使合适”，出自 aptus“合适的”。基本画面是一件东西被做成与另一件相配。

items.en: The suffix -ive comes from Latin -ivus, meaning 'tending to, having the nature of'. It turns adapt into a word for a capacity, not a completed action.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive 来自拉丁语 -ivus，意为“倾向于、具有……性质的”。它把 adapt 变成表示能力的词，而不是完成的动作。

items.en: Adaptive appears in English for things that tend to adapt. Early uses are general; biology later gives the word its strongest home.
items.cn: 18 世纪，adaptive 出现在英语中，指倾向于适应的东西。早期用法较一般，后来生物学给了这个词最稳固的归宿。

items.en: Evolutionary writing pairs adaptive with fitness: an adaptive trait is one that helps survival. The adjective becomes a judgement about value in an environment.
items.cn: 19 世纪的演化写作把 adaptive 与适应度配对：适应性状就是有助于生存的性状。这个形容词于是成为对“在某一环境中的价值”的判断。

items.en: Computing, immunology, architecture, and policy each adopt it for self-correcting systems. The common thread is a loop: measure, fit, measure again.
items.cn: 20 世纪，计算机、免疫学、建筑与政策各自采用它来指自我修正系统。共同线索是一个回路：测量、适合、再测量。

note.en: The first group shares the adapt- shape but differs in suffix; the second compares adjectives of flexibility.
note.cn: 第一组共享 adapt- 外形，但后缀不同；第二组比较表示“灵活”的形容词。

entries.definition: able to be changed to fit. It stresses the capacity of the object, while adaptive stresses the ongoing process or design.
entries.definitionCN: 能被改变以适合。它强调对象的容量，而 adaptive 强调持续的过程或设计。

entries.definition: the process or result of fitting. It is the noun, not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 适合的过程或结果。它是名词，不是形容词。

entries.definition: made suitable. It describes a completed fit, while adaptive describes a continuing capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 被改造成适合的。它描述已完成的适合，而 adaptive 描述持续的能力。

entries.definition: related to adoption. Its root is optare 'choose', not aptare 'fit'.
entries.definitionCN: 与收养有关的。其词根是 optare“选择”，不是 aptare“适合”。

entries.definition: able to bend or change easily. It is broader and physical as well as behavioural.
entries.definitionCN: 容易弯曲或改变的。它更宽泛，既指物理也指行为。

entries.definition: able to recover after stress or damage. It stresses bouncing back rather than fitting in.
entries.definitionCN: 在压力或损伤后能恢复。它强调回弹，而不是适合。

entries.definition: able to serve many purposes. It describes range, while adaptive describes response to conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 能用于多种目的。它描述用途范围，而 adaptive 描述对条件的反应。

entries.definition: reacting quickly and appropriately. It stresses the reaction, while adaptive stresses the resulting fit.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而适当地反应。它强调反应，而 adaptive 强调由此产生的适合。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on -ive as 'tending to' and the feedback loop, then three abstract images about a design that keeps fitting.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 -ive“倾向于”与反馈回路的挂钩，再用三个关于“持续适合的设计”的抽象画面。

normal.en: adapt + -ive = tending to fit: not fitted once, but built to keep fitting.
normal.cn: adapt + -ive = 倾向于适合：不是适合一次，而是被造来持续适合。

normal.en: Adaptable is the capacity; adaptive is the working disposition. A towel is adaptable, a thermostat is adaptive.
normal.cn: adaptable 是容量；adaptive 是运行中的倾向。毛巾是 adaptable，恒温器是 adaptive。

normal.en: Adaptive immunity is memory written into cells: the body edits itself after meeting a virus.
normal.cn: 适应性免疫是写进细胞的记忆：身体遇见病毒后编辑自己。

normal.en: Adaptive reuse keeps the warehouse and changes the purpose: the coat stays, the job changes.
normal.cn: 适应性再利用保留仓库、改变用途：外套还在，工作变了。

normal.en: Adaptive management is a plan that expects to be wrong and has a way to correct itself.
normal.cn: 适应性管理是一个预期自己会错、并且有办法自我纠正的计划。

abstract.en: An adaptive system pays for flexibility with predictability: it can meet anything, so it is hard to forecast.
abstract.cn: 自适应系统用可预测性换取灵活性：它能应对一切，因此难以预报。

abstract.en: Adaptive traits are local solutions: what fits here may be a liability there.
abstract.cn: 适应性状是地方性方案：在这里合身，在别处可能成为负担。

abstract.en: The word describes a relationship, not a possession: nothing is adaptive in the abstract, only to something.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述关系，而不是属性：没有东西抽象地“有适应性”，只对某物有。

examples.en: The course uses adaptive exercises that get harder as the student improves.
examples.cn: 这门课使用自适应练习，学生进步时会变难。

examples.en: Adaptive traits often arise from small genetic changes.
examples.cn: 适应性状常由微小的基因改变产生。

examples.en: The old mill's adaptive reuse preserved its water wheel.
examples.cn: 这座旧磨坊的适应性再利用保留了它的水车。

dict_mnemonic.note: adapt（使适合）+ -ive（倾向于）→ 倾向于持续适合的 → 有适应能力的。adaptable 是“能被改”，adaptive 是“自己在改”。
dict_mnemonic.text: adapt + -ive（有……倾向）→ 能持续调节以适合 → 适应的、自适应的

root: 拉丁 adaptare“使适合”（ad- + aptus 合适）+ 拉丁后缀 -ivus“倾向于” → 英语 adaptive（18 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one capacity through different systems: a team that adjusts, a trait that raises fitness, an immune system that remembers, a controller that corrects itself, flexible behaviour, a building refitted, a policy that learns, and a lineage that diversifies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项让同一种能力穿过不同系统：会调整的团队、提高适应度的性状、会记忆的免疫系统、自我修正的控制器、灵活的行为、被改用的建筑、会学习的政策，以及分化的谱系。

core.en: A suspension that changes stiffness as the ground changes beneath it
core.cn: 随脚下地面变化而改变软硬的悬挂

branches.en: A capacity in organizations and in behaviour: the team and the individual.
branches.cn: 组织与行为中的能力：团队与个人。

branches.en: THE TRAIT: a feature that raises an organism’s chance of surviving and reproducing.
branches.cn: 性状层面：提高生物生存与繁殖机会的性状。

branches.en: Learning systems: immune memory in cells, feedback memory in machines.
branches.cn: 学习系统：细胞里的免疫记忆，机器里的反馈记忆。

branches.en: Institutional fitting: a building given a new use, a policy revised by evidence.
branches.cn: 制度性的适合：建筑被赋予新用途，政策随证据修订。

branches.en: THE RADIATION: one adaptive burst opens many ecological niches.
branches.cn: 谱系的爆发：一次适应辐射打开许多生态位。

intro.en: Adaptive's family is built on adapt: the noun of process and result, the adverb, the capacity noun, and the negative maladaptive.
intro.cn: adaptive 的词族建立在 adapt 上：过程与结果名词、副词、能力名词，以及否定的 maladaptive。

latinIntro.en: Latin -ivus means 'tending to'. Attached to adaptare 'fit to', it yields a word for a disposition to fit. English also uses -able for capacity and -ation for the act, so the family divides the work neatly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -ivus 意为“倾向于”。接在 adaptare“使适合”上，产生表示“适合倾向”的词。英语还用 -able 表容量、-ation 表动作，因此词族分工清楚。

items.example: Adaptive software learns from use.
items.exampleCN: 自适应软件从使用中学习。

items.example: The plant adapts to shade.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物适应荫蔽。

items.meaning: the process or product of fitting
items.meaningCN: 适应过程或产物；改编作品
items.example: The adaptation took years.
items.exampleCN: 这一适应过程花了数年。

items.example: The animal responds adaptively to noise.
items.exampleCN: 这种动物对噪声作出适应性反应。

items.example: Adaptability varies between species.
items.exampleCN: 不同物种的适应能力不同。

items.example: The adaptiveness of the system impressed the team.
items.exampleCN: 系统的适应性让团队印象深刻。

items.example: Avoidance can be maladaptive.
items.exampleCN: 回避可能是一种适应不良。

items.example: An apt reply fits the moment.
items.exampleCN: 恰当的回答符合当下情境。

items.example: She showed an aptitude for languages.
items.exampleCN: 她显示出语言天赋。
